parents.text:
## Subject: Offer of Employment
Dear Rohan Dilip Sharma,
We are pleased to extend to you an offer of employment with Turabit Solutions as a Software Engineer at the Backend Mid-Level within our (L3) Engineering - Platform Team. You will be joining a dedicated group of eight engineers under the leadership of your Reporting Manager, Karan Joshi, Senior Engineering Manager.
Your anticipated joining date is 19 May 2026, which we hope will allow for a smooth transition into your new role. This position is offered on a full-time basis, reflecting our commitment to your professional growth and contribution to the company.Upon successful completion of your probation period, you will be eligible for a hybrid work arrangement, allowing three days in the office and two days remote work each week.
Your employment will commence with a probation period of three months from your date of joining. During this time, your performance will be evaluated based on criteria including timely delivery of assigned sprint tasks with at least an 80% completion rate, active participation in code reviews, adherence to engineering standards, absence of unresolved escalations, and satisfactory feedback from both your reporting manager and at least one peer. A formal probation review will be conducted by the Human Resources department and Karan Joshi at the conclusion of this period.
Please note that your employment is conditional upon successful completion of pre-employment verifications, including identity verification through Aadhaar or PAN, reference checks covering your last two years of employment, educational qualification verification, and a criminal background check conducted by our third-party vendor, AuthBridge. All required documents must be submitted to Human Resources on or before your joining date. Any discrepancies discovered after joining may result in immediate termination of employment.
As part of your role, you will be expected to maintain strict confidentiality regarding all proprietary information, client data, product roadmaps, source code, and business strategies both during and after your tenure with Turabit Solutions.
We kindly ask you to review this offer carefully and communicate your acceptance by 09 May 2026, following the instructions provided separately. Should you have any questions or require further clarification, please do not hesitate to contact our Human Resources team at hr@turabitsolutions.com.
We look forward to welcoming you to Turabit Solutions and are confident that your skills and experience will be a valuable addition to our team.
Sincerely,
Saakhi Desai , HR

parents.title: Learning and Development Policy
parents.breadcrumb: Learning and Development Policy > Purpose and Strategic Objectives
parents.text:
## Purpose and Strategic Objectives
The Learning and Development (L&D) policy at Turabit Solutions is designed to directly support the company's strategic ambition of becoming the most trusted SaaS partner for 10,000 businesses across South and Southeast Asia by 2030. Achieving this scale requires a workforce equipped with advanced technical skills, customer success expertise, and strong leadership capabilities. The policy aims to bridge the gap between current employee capabilities and the skills needed 18 months into the future to meet evolving business demands. Key strategic outcomes include reducing the time-to-productivity for new hires from 90 days to 60 days by the end of fiscal year 2027, ensuring that 80% of engineering roles have at least one certified specialist in their primary technology stack by the end of fiscal year 2026, and building an internal pipeline of 10 managers ready for senior leadership roles by fiscal year 2028. Additionally, the policy targets a 30% reduction in external hiring for senior positions by developing internal talent and achieving a minimum L&D satisfaction score of 4.2 out of 5 across all programs. Beyond capability building, the policy also addresses employee retention challenges, as exit interview data indicates that lack of growth opportunities is the second most cited reason for resignation. Structured learning and development initiatives are therefore critical to fostering employee engagement and long-term retention.

parents.title: Learning and Development Policy
parents.breadcrumb: Learning and Development Policy > Scope and Eligibility
parents.text:
## Scope and Eligibility
This policy applies comprehensively to all full-time permanent employees of Turabit Solutions from their first day of employment, encompassing all departments and levels ranging from L1 (Junior) to L7 (Director). Fixed-term contract employees with contracts of six months or longer are eligible to participate in self-paced online learning and internal knowledge-sharing sessions; however, they are not eligible for externally sponsored certifications or conference attendance unless explicitly approved by the respective department head and the Chief Financial Officer. Probationary employees have access exclusively to mandatory onboarding training and role-specific technical induction programs, with discretionary learning and development budgets becoming available only upon confirmation of employment. Interns may participate in internal knowledge-sharing sessions and utilize any free or low-cost online learning resources provided by the company. Part-time employees are eligible for learning and development opportunities on a pro-rated basis relative to their working hours. Third-party contractors and agency staff are excluded from all sponsored learning and development programs under this policy.

parents.title: Learning and Development Policy
parents.breadcrumb: Learning and Development Policy > Annual Training Needs Assessment Process
parents.text:
## Annual Training Needs Assessment Process
The Training Needs Assessment (TNA) is conducted annually during February and March to plan learning and development initiatives for the upcoming financial year. The process consists of four distinct stages to ensure a data-driven and comprehensive identification of capability gaps and training priorities.
Stage 1, Business Priority Mapping, occurs in the first two weeks of February, during which Human Resources meets with each department head and the CEO to review strategic priorities, new product initiatives, technology stack changes, regulatory requirements, and headcount plans. This collaboration produces a preliminary list of capability gaps at the department level.
Stage 2, Manager Input, takes place in the latter half of February. Reporting managers complete structured TNA forms in Keka for each direct report, assessing technical skills gaps relative to the next role level, behavioral competency gaps identified during the October appraisal, and any mandatory compliance training requirements. Managers are required to base their input on objective biannual performance review data rather than subjective impressions.
Stage 3, Employee Self-Assessment, occurs in the first week of March, where all confirmed employees complete a self-assessment in Keka, rating their proficiency against a standardized skills matrix for their role family and submitting their top three learning priorities for the year.
Stage 4, Consolidation and Prioritisation, happens in the second and third weeks of March. HR consolidates manager inputs and employee self-assessments, identifies overlapping needs suitable for group programs, and develops the Annual L&D Plan, including a training calendar and budget allocation by department. The finalized plan is reviewed and approved by the CEO by 31 March and implemented from 1 April.

parents.title: Learning and Development Policy
parents.breadcrumb: Learning and Development Policy > Types of Learning Programs
parents.text:
## Types of Learning Programs
Mandatory Compliance Training: This includes annual courses on Information Security Awareness, Prevention of Sexual Harassment, Data Privacy and GDPR basics for employees handling client data, and Fire Safety and Emergency Procedures for all office-based employees. Completion is tracked in Keka, and non-completion by the deadline is escalated to the respective department head.
Technical Certification Programs: These are company-sponsored external certifications in technologies such as AWS, GCP, Azure, Kubernetes, Python, Django, Salesforce, HubSpot, PMP, and ISTQB, depending on the employee's role. The company reimburses full fees upon passing the certification. The first attempt is sponsored upfront, while subsequent attempts require a 50% co-payment by the employee.
Online Self-Paced Learning: Turabit Solutions provides a company subscription to Udemy for Business accessible to all confirmed employees. Additionally, LinkedIn Learning access is available for employees at level L4 and above. Employees may enroll in any course relevant to their role without prior approval.
Instructor-Led Workshops: These are quarterly half-day or full-day workshops on topics identified through the Training Needs Assessment. Workshops are delivered by external trainers or senior internal subject matter experts. Topics for fiscal year 2026 include Advanced System Design, Managing Difficult Conversations, Data-Driven Customer Success, and Financial Acumen for Non-Finance Managers.

parents.title: Learning and Development Policy
parents.breadcrumb: Learning and Development Policy > Internal Training and Knowledge Sharing Sessions
parents.text:
## Internal Training and Knowledge Sharing Sessions
Turabit Solutions fosters a culture of continuous learning through a variety of internal training and knowledge-sharing initiatives designed to enhance technical expertise, cross-functional understanding, and team collaboration. Tech Talks are held every alternate Friday from 4:00 PM to 5:00 PM, where an engineer presents an in-depth exploration of a technical topic such as system design decisions, production incident post-mortems, new tool evaluations, or proofs of concept. Attendance is mandatory for the engineering team and open to all employees.
Presentations are recorded and uploaded to the internal Confluence page within 24 hours. Engineers are expected to present at least once every six months, with topic proposals submitted to the Engineering Manager by Wednesday of the presentation week. Product Demo Sessions occur on the first Thursday of every month, where Product Management delivers a 30-minute live demonstration of features shipped in the previous month and upcoming roadmap items. These sessions are mandatory for engineering, customer success, and sales teams and are recorded and shared on Slack for wider accessibility.
Cross-Functional Learning Hours are monthly one-hour sessions where a different department presents its functions, tools, and collaboration best practices to other teams. Organized by HR, these sessions rotate across departments to break down silos and improve interdepartmental cooperation. The Onboarding Buddy Program assigns every new joiner a peer within the same team who has at least one year of tenure. The buddy guides the new employee through team processes, tools, codebase conventions, and cultural norms during the first 30 days. Buddies receive a Rs 2,000 Flipkart voucher upon successful completion of the program, contingent on positive feedback from the new joiner.
Additionally, the Book Club is an optional quarterly initiative where HR purchases ten copies of a selected business or technology book chosen by employee vote. Participants read the book and convene for a one-hour discussion session at the end of the quarter, fostering informal learning and community building. Past titles include The Phoenix Project, Continuous Discovery Habits, and An Elegant Puzzle.

parents.title: Learning and Development Policy
parents.breadcrumb: Learning and Development Policy > External Training, Certification and Conference Support
parents.text:
## External Training, Certification and Conference Support
Turabit Solutions provides comprehensive support for external training, certification, and conference attendance to enhance employee skills and industry knowledge. Certification support is available to all confirmed employees from level L1 upwards. Employees or their managers identify certifications relevant to the current or next role in the career path. Eligibility requires that the certification be on the approved list maintained by HR or pre-approved by the department head if not listed. Employees submit a certification request form in Keka detailing the certification name, provider, cost, exam date, and relevance to their role. Reporting managers approve requests within five working days, followed by HR verification of budget availability.
Certifications costing above Rs 15,000 require additional CFO approval. The company covers registration fees and study material costs, and grants up to two days of study leave per certification attempt, which must be applied for in Keka. Exam fees for failed attempts are not sponsored for a second attempt without a six-month waiting period. Conference support is available to employees at level L4 and above. Eligible conferences must be directly relevant to the employee's role, and the employee must have a performance rating of 3 or higher.
Employees committing to attend must present a summary session to their team within two weeks of returning. Covered costs include registration fees, economy class travel, accommodation up to Rs 5,000 per night, and a per diem of Rs 2,500 per day. Expenses exceeding these limits require CFO approval. Employees may attend up to two domestic conferences per year and one international conference per year, with international attendance restricted to level L5 and above unless special approval is granted. For external instructor-led courses not covered under the certification program, the company reimburses up to Rs 15,000 per employee per year. Claims must be submitted via Keka Reimbursements with the course invoice and completion certificate within 30 days of course completion.

parents.title: Learning and Development Policy
parents.breadcrumb: Learning and Development Policy > Annual L&D Budget Allocation per Employee and Department
parents.text:
## Annual L&D Budget Allocation per Employee and Department
The annual Learning and Development (L&D) budget allocation at Turabit Solutions is structured to ensure targeted investment in employee skill enhancement aligned with the company's strategic objectives. Each confirmed employee is allocated a per capita learning budget of Rs 15,000 per financial year. This individual budget is intended to cover expenses related to certifications, external courses, and study materials. It is important to note that subscriptions to Udemy for Business and LinkedIn Learning are centrally provided and do not draw from this individual allocation.
In addition to the per-employee budget, each department receives a dedicated training budget to support group learning initiatives and specialized programs that address the unique needs of their teams. For the fiscal year 2026, the departmental budgets are as follows: Engineering is allocated Rs 3,00,000 annually to fund external workshops, bootcamps, and advanced technical training essential for maintaining cutting-edge expertise within the team. Customer Success has a budget of Rs 1,50,000 to support sales methodology training, customer success certifications such as Gainsight and Salesforce, and negotiation skills workshops. Product Management is assigned Rs 1,00,000 to facilitate product management certifications through AIPMM and Pragmatic Institute, as well as attendance at relevant product conferences. The Human Resources department receives Rs 75,000 to cover HR certifications including SHRM and NHRDN, employment law updates, and training on HR technologies. Finance is allocated Rs 50,000 to support accounting software training and CFO leadership development programs.
A significant investment is also made in leadership development, with a dedicated budget of Rs 5,00,000 per year for the Leadership Development Program cohort. This budget covers external facilitator fees, training materials, and assessments for up to 10 participants, reflecting the company's commitment to building a strong internal leadership pipeline.
Collectively, these allocations contribute to a total annual L&D budget of approximately Rs 20,00,000 for the financial year 2026. This budget is subject to approval by the Chief Financial Officer each April as part of the company's financial planning cycle. The structured allocation of funds ensures that both individual and departmental learning needs are met effectively, supporting Turabit Solutions' broader goal of closing capability gaps and fostering continuous employee development.

parents.title: Learning and Development Policy
parents.breadcrumb: Learning and Development Policy > Manager Nomination and Self-Nomination Process
parents.text:
## Manager Nomination and Self-Nomination Process
The nomination process for learning and development programs at Turabit Solutions involves both manager nominations and self-nominations to ensure broad access and alignment with individual career goals. During the Training Needs Assessment process in February and March, reporting managers identify employees within their teams who would benefit from specific programs in the upcoming year. Nominations are submitted in Keka by 31 March.
For the Leadership Development Program, managers may nominate a maximum of two employees per team. Each nomination must be supported by the employee's most recent performance rating, a written justification of at least 100 words, and confirmation that the employee has been informed of the nomination. HR reviews all nominations for eligibility and budget alignment and communicates confirmed nominations to managers by 15 April. Any confirmed employee may also self-nominate for any program listed on the annual training calendar by submitting a self-nomination form in Keka.
This form requires the program name, a minimum 100-word explanation of interest, and the relevance to the employee's current role or career objectives. Self-nominations are reviewed by the employee's reporting manager within five working days, who may approve, reject with a written reason, or recommend an alternative program. Employees may appeal rejected self-nominations to the HR Manager if they believe the rejection is unreasonable. For the Leadership Development Program, self-nominations are accepted alongside manager nominations and evaluated using the same criteria. Final selection for cohort-based programs is made by HR in consultation with department heads and announced by 30 April each year.

parents.title: Learning and Development Policy
parents.breadcrumb: Learning and Development Policy > Sponsorship Terms
parents.text:
## Sponsorship Terms
For any learning and development investment exceeding Rs 25,000 per employee per instance--including certifications, external courses, conference attendance, or any combination thereof--specific bond terms apply to safeguard the company's investment. The bond period is 12 months from the date of program completion. Should an employee voluntarily resign within this period, the company will recover a proportionate amount of the sponsored program cost from the full and final settlement as follows: 100% recovery if resignation occurs within three months of completion; 75% recovery if between three and six months; 50% recovery if between six and nine months; and 25% recovery if between nine and twelve months. No recovery is required if the employee is terminated by the company without cause. Employees must sign a Training Bond Agreement prior to payment or registration processing. Bond terms are clearly disclosed to employees at the time of nomination or self-nomination approval. For the Leadership Development Program, the bond period extends to 18 months due to the higher per-participant investment. Bond recovery is waived if the employee is transferred, promoted, or if the company undergoes a change of ownership.

parents.title: Learning and Development Policy
parents.breadcrumb: Learning and Development Policy > Post-Training Knowledge Transfer and Application Commitment
parents.text:
## Post-Training Knowledge Transfer and Application Commitment
Employees who complete external certifications, attend conferences, or participate in externally delivered workshops are required to fulfill specific post-training commitments within 30 days of program completion to ensure knowledge transfer and practical application. First, they must deliver a minimum 30-minute internal presentation to their team summarizing key learnings, tools or frameworks covered, and specific applications to current work. This presentation is scheduled by the reporting manager and recorded for inclusion in the Confluence knowledge base. Second, employees must submit a written application plan of at least 200 words in Keka within 15 days of program completion, detailing at least two specific ways the learning will be applied to current projects or processes within the next 90 days. Progress against this application plan is reviewed during the next quarterly check-in with the reporting manager. Participants in the Leadership Development Program have additional requirements, including submission of a 90-day action plan within one week of cohort completion and a retrospective presentation to the CEO and HR at the 90-day mark. Failure to complete these knowledge transfer requirements without a valid reason, such as a medical emergency or business travel, results in the program cost being reclassified as a personal development expense subject to recovery under the sponsorship terms.

parents.title: Learning and Development Policy
parents.breadcrumb: Learning and Development Policy > Learning Effectiveness Measurement and ROI Tracking
parents.text:
## Learning Effectiveness Measurement and ROI Tracking
Turabit Solutions employs a multi-level framework to measure learning effectiveness and track return on investment (ROI) for all learning and development programs. At the Reaction Level (Level 1), all participants complete a post-training feedback form in Keka within three days of program completion. This form evaluates trainer quality, content relevance, material quality, and overall satisfaction on a scale of 1 to 5. Programs scoring below a minimum acceptable satisfaction score of 3.8 for two consecutive cohorts are reviewed and either redesigned or discontinued. At the Learning Level (Level 2), HR tracks pass or fail results for technical certifications. For workshops, a short knowledge check consisting of ten questions is administered in Keka within one week of the session, with a pass mark of 70%.
Employees scoring below 70% are offered remedial resources and a recheck within two weeks. At the Behaviour Level (Level 3), reporting managers complete a behavioural change observation form in Keka 90 days post-training, assessing whether the employee is visibly applying learned skills on the job. This is rated on a three-point scale: not observed, partially observed, or consistently observed, with results recorded in the employee's L&D profile.
At the Results Level (Level 4), HR annually tracks key metrics and presents findings in the April L&D Review to the CEO. Metrics include reduction in external hiring for roles targeted by internal upskilling, changes in performance ratings of program participants versus non-participants, certification achievement rates with a target of 80% pass rate on the first attempt, reduction in time-to-productivity for new hires, and employee retention rates comparing those who participated in at least one L&D program against those who did not. The ROI report is presented to the CEO and CFO alongside the budget request for the following year.

parents.title: Learning and Development Policy
parents.breadcrumb: Learning and Development Policy > Career Development Pathways and Individual Development Plans
parents.text:
## Career Development Pathways and Individual Development Plans
Turabit Solutions maintains a published Career Framework on Confluence that defines all role families--Engineering, Product, Customer Success, Sales, HR, and Finance--and levels within each family from L1 to L7. This framework outlines the technical and behavioural competencies required at each level and is reviewed annually in March. Employees have clear visibility of expectations at their current and next levels, facilitating transparent promotion discussions. Additionally, every confirmed employee collaborates with their reporting manager annually in April to create an Individual Development Plan (IDP). The IDP identifies current strengths and development areas based on the October appraisal, sets two to three specific learning goals aligned with career framework competencies for the next level, and specifies learning programs or activities to address each goal. Milestones and completion dates are established, and managers commit to providing opportunities to apply learning through projects, responsibilities, or exposure. IDPs are reviewed quarterly during one-on-one meetings and formally assessed in the October appraisal. Completion of at least two out of three goals is a key input for promotion recommendations. Employees without an active IDP are flagged to their department head by HR in July.

parents.title: Learning and Development Policy
parents.breadcrumb: Learning and Development Policy > Policy Review Cycle and Approval Authority
parents.text:
## Policy Review Cycle and Approval Authority
This Learning and Development policy shall be reviewed annually each March to align with the Training Needs Assessment process and the fiscal year planning cycle.
Trigger-based reviews shall be conducted if any of the following conditions occur: a significant change in company size, defined as a headcount increase or decrease exceeding 25%; a new strategic direction requiring capabilities not currently addressed by the policy; changes in applicable employment regulations affecting training obligations; or feedback from the annual L&D satisfaction survey indicating an overall score below 3.5 out of 5.
The review process shall be led by the HR Manager, who shall draft proposed changes in consultation with department heads and the Chief Financial Officer, particularly for budgetary implications.
The draft revisions shall be circulated to all relevant stakeholders for feedback and incorporated as appropriate.
Final approval authority for the policy rests with the Chief Executive Officer, who shall review the proposed changes and formally approve the updated policy before implementation.
The approved policy shall be communicated to all employees via official channels and uploaded to the company intranet.
Compliance with the policy shall be monitored continuously, and any deviations shall be reported to the HR Manager for corrective action.

parents.title: Exit and Offboarding Policy
parents.breadcrumb: Exit and Offboarding Policy > Purpose and Scope
parents.text:
## Purpose and Scope
This Exit and Offboarding Policy establishes a clear and structured framework for managing employee separations at Turabit solutions. It aims to ensure that all separations, whether voluntary or involuntary, are handled professionally, consistently, and in compliance with applicable laws and company standards. The policy covers the entire separation process, including resignation submission, notice period obligations, clearance procedures, and the full and final settlement of dues. By defining these processes, the policy seeks to protect the interests of both the company and its employees while maintaining operational continuity.
The scope of this policy applies to all employees across all roles and bands within Turabit solutions, located in Pune. It addresses various types of separations such as resignations, terminations, retirements, and mutual separations. The policy also outlines the responsibilities of employees, managers, and the Human Resources department during the offboarding process to ensure a smooth transition.
Furthermore, this policy emphasizes the importance of knowledge transfer, asset return, and system access revocation to safeguard company resources and intellectual property. It also details the procedures for conducting exit interviews and issuing relevant documentation such as experience and relieving letters. Overall, this policy is designed to facilitate respectful and efficient employee separations that uphold Turabit solutions' values and operational requirements.

parents.title: Exit and Offboarding Policy
parents.breadcrumb: Exit and Offboarding Policy > Types of Separation
parents.text:
## Types of Separation
Voluntary Resignation: An employee-initiated separation where the individual submits a formal resignation to leave the company. This type requires adherence to notice period and clearance procedures as defined in this policy.
Involuntary Termination: Separation initiated by the company due to performance issues, misconduct, redundancy, or other business reasons. This includes both disciplinary and non-disciplinary terminations and follows legal and company guidelines.
Retirement: Separation due to an employee reaching the company's defined retirement age or opting for early retirement. Retirement processes include appropriate documentation and benefits settlement.
Mutual Separation: A consensual agreement between the employee and the company to part ways under mutually agreed terms. This may include negotiated notice periods, settlements, and other conditions.

parents.title: Exit and Offboarding Policy
parents.breadcrumb: Exit and Offboarding Policy > Resignation Submission Process and Acceptance Protocol
parents.text:
## Resignation Submission Process and Acceptance Protocol
Employees intending to resign must submit a formal resignation letter addressed to their immediate supervisor and copied to the Human Resources department. The resignation letter should clearly state the intended last working day, adhering to the notice period requirements specified in this policy. The submission can be made in writing or via the company's designated HR portal, ensuring a verifiable record of the resignation.
Upon receipt of the resignation, the supervisor shall acknowledge the resignation in writing within two business days and initiate the acceptance process. The Human Resources department will review the resignation to confirm compliance with notice period obligations and initiate the offboarding workflow. Any discrepancies or concerns regarding the resignation date or notice period shall be communicated promptly to the employee for resolution.
The acceptance of resignation is formalized through an official acceptance letter issued by Human Resources, which confirms the last working day and outlines the next steps in the offboarding process. This letter serves as an official record and is shared with payroll, IT, and other relevant departments to coordinate clearance and settlement activities.
Employees are encouraged to engage in open communication with their supervisors and HR during this process to ensure a smooth transition. Failure to follow the resignation submission and acceptance protocol may result in delays in clearance and final settlement processing.

parents.title: Exit and Offboarding Policy
parents.breadcrumb: Exit and Offboarding Policy > Notice Period Requirements by Role and Band
parents.text:
## Notice Period Requirements by Role and Band
All employees must provide a written notice of resignation in accordance with their designated notice period based on role and band classification.
Entry-level and junior band employees shall provide a minimum notice period of 30 calendar days.
Mid-level and specialist band employees shall provide a minimum notice period of 60 calendar days.
Senior management and leadership band employees shall provide a minimum notice period of 90 calendar days.
Notice periods must be served in full unless otherwise agreed in writing by the company through the early release or buyout provisions.
Employees shall continue to perform their duties diligently during the notice period and cooperate with knowledge transfer and handover activities.
Failure to serve the full notice period without company consent may result in deductions from the final settlement as per company policy.
The company reserves the right to waive or reduce the notice period at its discretion, subject to operational requirements and mutual agreement.
Notice period obligations apply equally to voluntary resignations and mutual separations unless otherwise specified in the separation agreement.

parents.title: Exit and Offboarding Policy
parents.breadcrumb: Exit and Offboarding Policy > Notice Period Buyout and Early Release Conditions
parents.text:
## Notice Period Buyout and Early Release Conditions
Turabit solutions recognizes that circumstances may arise where an employee requests early release from their notice period or wishes to buy out the remaining notice period. Such requests shall be considered on a case-by-case basis, balancing the employee's needs with the company's operational requirements.
Employees seeking early release must submit a formal written request to Human Resources, detailing the reasons for the request and the proposed last working day. The company shall evaluate the impact of the early release on ongoing projects, team capacity, and knowledge transfer obligations before making a decision.
Notice period buyout involves the employee compensating the company for the unserved portion of the notice period. The buyout amount is calculated based on the employee's gross salary for the remaining notice days. This amount must be paid in full before the employee's last working day, and the company will provide a formal invoice for the same.
Approval of early release or notice period buyout is at the sole discretion of the company and requires written confirmation from Human Resources and the employee's reporting manager. If approved, the employee must complete all clearance formalities and knowledge transfer activities before departure.
In cases where early release or buyout is not approved, the employee is expected to serve the full notice period as per policy. Non-compliance may affect the issuance of relieving documents and final settlement processing.

parents.title: Exit and Offboarding Policy
parents.breadcrumb: Exit and Offboarding Policy > Knowledge Transfer Plan and Handover Documentation
parents.text:
## Knowledge Transfer Plan and Handover Documentation
A comprehensive knowledge transfer plan is mandatory for all employees undergoing separation to ensure continuity of work and minimize disruption. The departing employee shall collaborate with their manager to identify critical tasks, ongoing projects, and key contacts that require handover.
The knowledge transfer plan must include detailed documentation of current responsibilities, project statuses, process workflows, and any pending deliverables. This documentation should be clear, accessible, and stored in the company's designated repositories to facilitate easy reference by successors or team members.
Employees are required to conduct formal handover sessions with designated colleagues or successors, providing verbal explanations and answering queries to clarify any ambiguities. These sessions should be scheduled well in advance of the last working day to allow adequate time for knowledge absorption.
Managers are responsible for monitoring the progress of the knowledge transfer and ensuring that all necessary information is captured and shared. Any gaps or concerns must be addressed promptly to avoid operational risks.
Failure to complete the knowledge transfer plan satisfactorily may delay clearance and final settlement. The company reserves the right to withhold relieving documentation until all handover requirements are fulfilled.

parents.title: Exit and Offboarding Policy
parents.breadcrumb: Exit and Offboarding Policy > System, Tool and Repository Access Revocation Checklist
parents.text:
## System, Tool and Repository Access Revocation Checklist
To protect company data and maintain security, all system, tool, and repository access granted to the departing employee must be revoked promptly upon separation. The IT department, in coordination with Human Resources, will manage the access revocation process.
The checklist includes but is not limited to access to email accounts, internal communication platforms, project management tools, code repositories, cloud storage, VPNs, and any third-party applications used for business operations. The employee's access rights shall be reviewed and disabled effective from the last working day or earlier if required.
Managers must provide a list of systems and tools accessed by the employee to the IT department at least five business days before the separation date. This enables timely preparation for access revocation.
The IT department will confirm the completion of access revocation to Human Resources, which will be documented as part of the clearance process. Any exceptions or delays must be escalated immediately to ensure compliance.Employees are prohibited from attempting to access company systems after their last working day. Unauthorized access attempts will be subject to disciplinary action and legal consequences.

parents.title: Exit and Offboarding Policy
parents.breadcrumb: Exit and Offboarding Policy > Company Asset and Equipment Return Process
parents.text:
## Company Asset and Equipment Return Process
All company assets and equipment issued to the employee during their tenure must be returned in good working condition before the completion of the clearance process. This includes laptops, mobile devices, access cards, keys, software licenses, and any other property belonging to Turabit solutions.
Employees are required to submit a complete list of issued assets to their manager and Human Resources at least ten business days prior to their last working day. The return of assets shall be coordinated with the Facilities or IT department, depending on the nature of the items.
A formal asset return checklist will be used to verify the condition and completeness of returned items. Any damage, loss, or missing assets must be reported immediately, and the employee may be held financially responsible as per company policy.
The asset return must be completed before the issuance of relieving and experience letters. Failure to return company property may result in withholding of final settlement and legal action if necessary.Managers and HR representatives shall ensure that the asset return process is documented and signed off by all parties involved to maintain clear records.

parents.title: Exit and Offboarding Policy
parents.breadcrumb: Exit and Offboarding Policy > No-Dues Clearance Process Across All Departments
parents.text:
## No-Dues Clearance Process Across All Departments
The no-dues clearance process is a critical step in the offboarding procedure to confirm that the departing employee has fulfilled all financial, operational, and administrative obligations. This process involves obtaining clearance certificates from all relevant departments including Finance, IT, Facilities, and any other business units involved.
Human Resources will initiate the clearance process upon acceptance of resignation or separation notice. Each department will verify that the employee has returned all assets, settled any outstanding dues, completed knowledge transfer, and complied with company policies.
The employee must coordinate with the designated department representatives to resolve any pending issues promptly. Delays or disputes in clearance may impact the timing of the full and final settlement and issuance of relieving documents.
A consolidated no-dues clearance form will be maintained by Human Resources, documenting approvals from all departments. This form must be signed off before the employee's exit is finalized.
The company reserves the right to deduct any outstanding amounts from the employee's final settlement if clearance is not obtained voluntarily. Clear communication and cooperation during this process are essential to ensure a smooth separation.

parents.title: Exit and Offboarding Policy
parents.breadcrumb: Exit and Offboarding Policy > Full and Final Settlement Calculation and Payment Timeline
parents.text:
## Full and Final Settlement Calculation and Payment Timeline
The full and final settlement process at Turabit Solutions is designed to ensure a comprehensive and transparent closure of all financial and administrative obligations between the company and the departing employee. This process encompasses the calculation and disbursement of all dues, including unpaid salary, leave encashment, applicable bonuses, and any other monetary entitlements. Concurrently, necessary deductions are applied, such as those related to notice period shortfall, tax liabilities, or costs associated with asset recovery, in accordance with the company's policies and relevant legal requirements.
To facilitate a smooth transition and uphold compliance, the settlement calculation is conducted only after the employee has completed all exit formalities, including the mandatory knowledge transfer, return of company assets, and clearance of all dues through the no-dues process. This clearance involves obtaining approvals from multiple departments such as IT, Finance, Administration, and the employee's reporting manager, each verifying that there are no outstanding responsibilities or obligations. Only upon receipt of these approvals does Human Resources proceed with the settlement.
Turabit Solutions commits to processing and disbursing the full and final settlement within a defined timeline following the employee's last working day, ensuring adherence to applicable labor laws and internal standards. Payments are made directly to the employee's registered bank account to maintain security and efficiency. Alongside the payment, a detailed settlement statement is provided to the employee, outlining all components of the calculation, including earnings, deductions, and net payable amounts, thereby promoting transparency and clarity.
This structured approach to full and final settlement not only safeguards the company's interests by ensuring all financial and asset-related matters are resolved but also provides departing employees with a professional and respectful exit experience. It reflects Turabit Solutions' commitment to maintaining operational continuity and protecting company assets and data throughout the offboarding process.

parents.title: Exit and Offboarding Policy
parents.breadcrumb: Exit and Offboarding Policy > Exit Interview Process and Feedback Collection
parents.text:
## Exit Interview Process and Feedback Collection
An exit interview is conducted with every departing employee to gather valuable feedback on their experience at Turabit solutions and identify areas for organizational improvement. The Human Resources department schedules the exit interview during the employee's notice period, preferably before the last working day.
The interview may be conducted in person, via video call, or through a structured questionnaire, depending on the circumstances and employee preference. The discussion covers topics such as reasons for leaving, job satisfaction, workplace environment, management support, and suggestions for improvement.
All feedback collected during the exit interview is treated confidentially and used solely for enhancing company policies, culture, and employee engagement. The HR team compiles anonymized reports for senior management review.
Employees are encouraged to provide honest and constructive feedback. Participation in the exit interview is a key part of the offboarding process and may influence the issuance of relieving documentation.The exit interview also serves as an opportunity to clarify any outstanding questions regarding final settlement, benefits, and post-employment obligations.

parents.title: Exit and Offboarding Policy
parents.breadcrumb: Exit and Offboarding Policy > Issuance of Experience Letter, Relieving Letter and Reference Policy
parents.text:
## Issuance of Experience Letter, Relieving Letter and Reference Policy
Upon successful completion of the clearance and offboarding process, Turabit solutions will issue an Experience Letter and a Relieving Letter to the departing employee. The Experience Letter will detail the employee's role, tenure, and key contributions, while the Relieving Letter will confirm that the employee has been formally relieved from their duties.
These documents are provided within 15 calendar days following the employee's last working day, contingent upon fulfillment of all clearance requirements. The company maintains a policy of providing factual and professional references upon request, subject to prior approval by Human Resources.
Employees are advised to request these documents through the HR department. Any discrepancies or delays should be communicated promptly for resolution.

parents.title: Exit and Offboarding Policy
parents.breadcrumb: Exit and Offboarding Policy > Post-Employment Obligations and Approval
parents.text:
## Post-Employment Obligations and Approval
Employees shall maintain confidentiality of all proprietary and sensitive information acquired during their employment with Turabit solutions and shall not disclose such information to any third party.
Former employees must not engage in any activities that conflict with the company's interests or compete directly with Turabit solutions for a period as defined in their employment agreement or applicable law.
Any intellectual property created during the course of employment remains the exclusive property of Turabit solutions, and former employees shall not use or distribute such property without prior written consent.
Employees shall return or destroy any confidential documents or materials in their possession upon request by the company after separation.
Compliance with non-solicitation and non-compete clauses, if applicable, is mandatory and monitored by the company.
The company reserves the right to take legal action in case of breach of post-employment obligations.
All post-employment obligations must be acknowledged and agreed upon by the employee as part of the separation process.
Managers and Human Resources shall ensure that these obligations are clearly communicated and documented during offboarding.

parents.title: Employee Onboarding SOP
parents.breadcrumb: Employee Onboarding SOP > Purpose
parents.text:
## Purpose
The primary purpose of the employee onboarding process at Turabit Solutions is to ensure that every new hire is smoothly integrated into the organization, aligned with its culture, and equipped to contribute effectively from the earliest possible stage. In a SaaS business environment where speed, collaboration, and product understanding are critical, onboarding serves as a structured bridge between hiring and productivity. It helps employees understand the company's products, customer expectations, workflows, and performance standards while reducing time-to-productivity and early attrition. By enabling new hires to quickly grasp how their role impacts product delivery, customer success, and revenue growth, onboarding directly supports Turabit Solutions' broader business objectives of scalability, customer retention, and continuous innovation. This process is designed to create a welcoming and informative experience that fosters engagement and commitment from day one. It also establishes a foundation for ongoing development and alignment with company goals, ensuring that employees feel valued and prepared to meet their responsibilities. Ultimately, the onboarding process is a critical investment in both the employee's success and the company's sustained growth.

parents.title: Employee Onboarding SOP
parents.breadcrumb: Employee Onboarding SOP > Scope
parents.text:
## Scope
This onboarding SOP applies to all employees joining Turabit Solutions, including full-time, part-time, contractual, and internship roles across all departments such as Engineering, Product, Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, Operations, and Support functions. It is designed to cover both technical and non-technical roles and is applicable across all work arrangements, including in-office, hybrid, and remote employees. The SOP ensures consistency in onboarding experience regardless of role or location while allowing for role-specific customization where required. By encompassing all categories of employment and work settings, the SOP provides a comprehensive framework that supports the diverse needs of the organization. It also facilitates compliance with internal standards and external regulations by standardizing key onboarding activities. This inclusive scope ensures that every new hire receives the necessary information, resources, and support to integrate successfully into Turabit Solutions, fostering a unified and productive workforce.

parents.title: Employee Onboarding SOP
parents.breadcrumb: Employee Onboarding SOP > Onboarding Objectives
parents.text:
## Onboarding Objectives
The onboarding process is intended to achieve several key outcomes that collectively ensure successful employee integration. It aims to familiarize new hires with the company's mission, vision, and operating principles, while also providing clarity on their individual roles, responsibilities, and performance expectations. It ensures that employees gain a foundational understanding of Turabit Solutions' SaaS products, target customers, and market positioning. Additionally, the process is designed to build early engagement, establish strong working relationships with team members, and enable employees to begin contributing meaningful work within a defined timeframe. Ultimately, onboarding should reduce confusion, accelerate learning, and create a sense of belonging and accountability. These objectives support both the employee's personal development and the company's strategic goals by fostering alignment and motivation. By meeting these objectives, Turabit Solutions ensures that new hires are well-prepared to deliver value and grow within the organization.

parents.title: Employee Onboarding SOP
parents.breadcrumb: Employee Onboarding SOP > Roles and Responsibilities
parents.text:
## Roles and Responsibilities
The onboarding process involves coordinated efforts from multiple stakeholders, each with clearly defined responsibilities to ensure a seamless and effective integration of new employees.
1. The Human Resources (HR) team must manage the overall onboarding workflow. This includes issuing offer letters, collecting and verifying employee documentation, communicating company policies, and ensuring compliance with organizational standards and legal requirements. HR shall also coordinate pre-joining communications and schedule orientation sessions.
2. Hiring Managers must take accountability for role-specific onboarding activities. They shall define initial tasks, set clear expectations, and provide guidance to help the new hire integrate into the team. Hiring Managers must also develop the first week's plan, including meetings, training sessions, and deliverables, to provide clarity and direction.
3. The IT or Systems team must provision all necessary system access and configure tools required for the employee's role. They shall ensure that access is granted based on the principle of least privilege and that technical setups such as email accounts, communication platforms, and product environments are ready before the employee's start date.
4. Team Members and Assigned Buddies shall support the new hire by helping them understand day-to-day workflows, team culture, and informal practices. They must be available to answer questions and facilitate social integration.
5. Senior Leadership may participate in orientation sessions to communicate strategic direction, company values, and foster a sense of purpose. Their involvement helps reinforce the importance of the onboarding process and motivates new employees. Each stakeholder must collaborate closely and escalate any issues or delays to HR to maintain the onboarding schedule and quality. Clear communication and accountability at every stage are essential to achieving the onboarding objectives and ensuring a positive employee experience.

parents.title: Employee Onboarding SOP
parents.breadcrumb: Employee Onboarding SOP > Pre Onboarding Preparation
parents.text:
## Pre Onboarding Preparation
Before the employee's first day, HR and hiring managers must complete several preparatory steps to ensure a seamless onboarding experience. This preparation begins with issuing the offer letter and confirming the candidate's acceptance to secure their commitment. HR is responsible for preparing a detailed onboarding schedule that outlines key activities, meetings, and training sessions planned for the initial period. Coordination with the IT team is essential to arrange system access and technical setup in advance. The employee's workstation, whether physical or remote, must be fully equipped and ready for use, including hardware, software, and network connectivity. Email accounts and essential communication tools should be created and tested to avoid delays on day one. HR must also send pre-joining communications such as welcome emails, joining instructions, and a checklist of required documentation to help the new hire prepare adequately. Hiring managers should define the first week's plan, including introductory meetings with team members, training sessions, and initial deliverables, to provide clarity and direction. This preparation phase is critical to creating a positive first impression and enabling the new employee to start productively without administrative or technical obstacles. By thoroughly completing these steps, Turabit Solutions ensures that new hires feel welcomed, informed, and ready to engage from their first day.

parents.title: Employee Onboarding SOP
parents.breadcrumb: Employee Onboarding SOP > Employee Documentation Collection
parents.text:
## Employee Documentation Collection
During onboarding, it is essential to collect and verify all required employee documentation to ensure legal and organizational compliance. This process typically includes obtaining identity proof, address proof, educational certificates, prior employment records, and bank details necessary for payroll processing. Depending on regulatory requirements and the employee's role, additional documents such as tax identification numbers, signed employment agreements, confidentiality agreements, and background verification forms must also be collected. HR is responsible for communicating the documentation requirements clearly to the new hire and verifying the authenticity and completeness of all submitted materials. Proper documentation safeguards the company from legal risks and supports compliance with labor laws and internal audit standards. It also facilitates accurate record-keeping and smooth administrative processing. The documentation collection process should be conducted with confidentiality and respect for employee privacy, ensuring secure handling and storage of sensitive information. Timely completion of this step is critical to avoid delays in payroll, benefits enrollment, and access provisioning. By maintaining a thorough and organized documentation process, Turabit Solutions upholds its commitment to regulatory compliance and operational excellence.

parents.title: Employee Onboarding SOP
parents.breadcrumb: Employee Onboarding SOP > System and Tool Access Setup
parents.text:
## System and Tool Access Setup
New employees must be provided with access to all necessary systems and tools required for their role to ensure they can begin work without delay. This includes setting up official email accounts, communication platforms such as chat and video conferencing tools, project management software, CRM systems, code repositories, cloud platforms, and any product-specific environments relevant to their responsibilities. Access levels must be granted based on the principle of least privilege to maintain security and data integrity. The IT team is responsible for provisioning these accesses promptly and securely, coordinating closely with hiring managers to identify role-specific tools and permissions in advance. This setup process also involves configuring hardware, installing required software, and ensuring network connectivity. Proper system access setup enables employees to perform their tasks efficiently from day one and supports adherence to cybersecurity standards. Any issues or delays in access provisioning must be escalated immediately to HR and IT leadership to resolve them quickly. By ensuring comprehensive and secure access to all necessary tools, Turabit Solutions facilitates a smooth transition for new hires into their operational roles.

parents.title: Employee Onboarding SOP
parents.breadcrumb: Employee Onboarding SOP > Orientation Process
parents.text:
## Orientation Process
The orientation process is designed to introduce new hires to Turabit Solutions' culture, structure, and operational framework. It typically begins with an overview of the company's history, mission, vision, and core values to provide context and inspire alignment. New employees are introduced to leadership and key teams to foster connections and understanding of organizational roles. Orientation includes detailed briefings on the company's SaaS products, target market, and customer segments to give business context and clarify how each role contributes to overall success. Additionally, employees are informed about organizational policies, communication norms, workplace expectations, and compliance requirements. This phase is critical in setting the tone for the employee's journey, helping them understand the company's strategic direction and their place within it. Orientation sessions may be conducted through presentations, interactive discussions, and Q&A opportunities to engage new hires fully. By providing a comprehensive introduction, Turabit Solutions ensures that employees feel welcomed, informed, and motivated to contribute effectively from the outset.

parents.title: Employee Onboarding SOP
parents.breadcrumb: Employee Onboarding SOP > Training and Initial Tasks
parents.text:
## Training and Initial Tasks
New employees are required to undergo structured training tailored to their specific roles to build the necessary skills and knowledge for effective performance. This training includes product education to understand Turabit Solutions' SaaS platform, technical training for engineering roles, and process or workflow training for business functions such as sales, marketing, or customer success. In addition to formal training modules, employees are assigned initial tasks or projects that allow them to apply their learning in a controlled environment. These tasks are designed to build confidence, encourage problem-solving, and provide early exposure to real work scenarios. Continuous feedback is provided during this phase to monitor progress, address challenges, and reinforce learning. Hiring managers and trainers collaborate to ensure that training content is relevant, up-to-date, and aligned with business objectives. This approach accelerates the employee's ability to contribute meaningfully and supports their professional development. By combining structured training with practical assignments, Turabit Solutions fosters a productive and engaging onboarding experience that prepares new hires for long-term success.

parents.title: Employee Onboarding SOP
parents.breadcrumb: Employee Onboarding SOP > Policy Acknowledgement
parents.text:
## Policy Acknowledgement
As part of the onboarding process, employees must review and formally acknowledge all key company policies to ensure awareness and compliance. 1. Employees shall review the Code of Conduct, which outlines expected professional behavior and ethical standards. 2. They must acknowledge data privacy and confidentiality policies to safeguard sensitive information and protect customer and company data. 3. Information security guidelines must be understood and accepted to maintain the integrity and security of IT systems and data. 4. Employees shall review anti-harassment and Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH) policies to promote a safe and respectful workplace environment. 5. Any additional relevant organizational policies, such as attendance, leave, and remote work guidelines, must also be acknowledged. Acknowledgement is typically documented through signed declarations or digital confirmations within the HR system. This formal process ensures that employees are fully informed of their responsibilities and the standards they are expected to uphold. It also provides a record of compliance that supports organizational governance and risk management. HR is responsible for facilitating policy communication and maintaining acknowledgement records. By enforcing thorough policy acknowledgement, Turabit Solutions fosters a culture of accountability and legal compliance.

parents.title: Employee Onboarding SOP
parents.breadcrumb: Employee Onboarding SOP > Onboarding Completion Checklist
parents.text:
## Onboarding Completion Checklist
The onboarding process is considered complete only after all predefined milestones have been met and verified to ensure a consistent and thorough integration experience. This includes the successful collection and verification of all required employee documentation, confirming legal and organizational compliance. System access setup must be fully provisioned, enabling the employee to perform their role without technical barriers. Orientation sessions should be completed, providing the new hire with a comprehensive understanding of the company's culture, products, and policies. Required training programs must be finished, equipping the employee with the necessary skills and knowledge. The employee must have clarity on their role and responsibilities, demonstrated through active participation in team activities and assignment of initial tasks. Feedback from both the employee and the hiring manager is collected to assess the effectiveness of the onboarding experience and identify areas for improvement. A formal checklist is maintained by HR to track completion of each step and ensure no critical element is overlooked. This structured approach guarantees that every new hire receives a consistent, high-quality onboarding experience that supports their success and engagement within Turabit Solutions.

parents.title: Employee Onboarding SOP
parents.breadcrumb: Employee Onboarding SOP > Approval
parents.text:
## Approval
This Employee Onboarding SOP for Turabit Solutions requires formal approval from authorized leadership to validate its alignment with organizational goals and compliance standards. The document must be reviewed and approved by the Head of Human Resources, the Chief Operating Officer or an equivalent senior executive, and, where applicable, members of the executive management team. Their approval confirms that the onboarding process is standardized, comprehensive, and supports the company's strategic direction. Upon approval, this SOP will be implemented across all departments and employment types to ensure consistency and effectiveness in onboarding new employees. Leadership is requested to review the document thoroughly and provide their signatures and dates below to formalize this approval.

parents.title: Payroll Policy
parents.breadcrumb: Payroll Policy > Purpose and Scope
parents.text:
## Purpose and Scope
This Payroll Policy document establishes the framework and guidelines for the administration of employee compensation at Turabit solutions. It aims to ensure a transparent, consistent, and compliant approach to salary structuring, payroll processing, statutory deductions, and related financial transactions. The policy applies to all employees across all departments and locations, including the Pune office, and covers all aspects of payroll management from salary credit to final settlement.
The purpose of this policy is to define the roles, responsibilities, and processes involved in payroll management to maintain accuracy, timeliness, and confidentiality. It also outlines the procedures for handling variable pay components, statutory deductions, tax computations, expense reimbursements, and dispute resolution mechanisms. This ensures that employees receive their rightful compensation in accordance with applicable laws and company standards.
Scope includes the entire payroll cycle, from salary calculation to payslip distribution, advance salary requests, salary revisions, and final settlements upon termination or resignation. The policy also governs compliance with statutory requirements and internal audit processes to uphold integrity and accountability in payroll operations. By adhering to this policy, Turabit solutions commits to fostering employee trust and satisfaction through fair and efficient payroll practices.

parents.title: Payroll Policy
parents.breadcrumb: Payroll Policy > Payroll Processing Cycle and Salary Credit Dates
parents.text:
## Payroll Processing Cycle and Salary Credit Dates
Payroll processing at Turabit Solutions Private Limited follows a monthly cycle, with the payroll input period spanning from the 26th of the preceding month to the 25th of the current month. All relevant data--including attendance, leave records, reimbursement claims, variable pay approvals, new joiner information, and separation details--must be submitted to the payroll team by the 25th without exception. Payroll processing is completed between the 26th and 27th of each month. The Finance department releases the salary transfer file to the bank on the 27th, and salaries are credited to employee accounts on the 28th of each month. If the 28th falls on a weekend or public holiday, salary credit occurs on the immediately preceding working day. December payroll operates on an accelerated schedule, with inputs due by 22nd December and salary credited by 26th December to accommodate the year-end holiday period. This schedule ensures timely and accurate salary disbursement in compliance with company standards and applicable regulations.

parents.title: Payroll Policy
parents.breadcrumb: Payroll Policy > Salary Structure Components
parents.text:
## Salary Structure Components
The salary structure at Turabit solutions is composed of multiple components designed to provide a comprehensive and competitive compensation package. The primary components include Basic Salary, House Rent Allowance (HRA), Special Allowance, and other applicable allowances. Basic Salary forms the core of the compensation and is the basis for calculating various statutory contributions and benefits.
House Rent Allowance is provided to employees to support their housing expenses and is calculated as a percentage of the Basic Salary. Special Allowance covers additional benefits and incentives that are not categorized under other heads and may vary based on role and performance. Other allowances may include conveyance, medical, and other statutory or company-specific benefits.
Each component is structured to comply with applicable labor laws and tax regulations, ensuring that employees receive fair remuneration while optimizing tax benefits. The salary components are reviewed periodically to align with market standards and company financial policies. Detailed breakdowns of each component are provided in the employee's offer letter and payslip for transparency and clarity.

parents.title: Payroll Policy
parents.breadcrumb: Payroll Policy > Variable Pay, Incentives and Commission Calculation Rules
parents.text:
## Variable Pay, Incentives and Commission Calculation Rules
Turabit solutions shall provide variable pay components including incentives and commissions based on individual and company performance metrics.
Variable pay shall be calculated monthly or quarterly as per the terms defined in the employee's contract or incentive plan.
Incentives must be linked to clearly defined Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and shall be approved by the respective department heads before disbursement.
Commissions shall be calculated based on sales or business generation figures verified by the sales operations team.
All variable pay calculations shall be subject to verification by the payroll department to ensure accuracy and compliance with company policies.
Variable pay shall be disbursed along with the regular salary on the designated salary credit date unless otherwise specified.
Any disputes or discrepancies in variable pay calculations must be reported within 15 days of payslip issuance for timely resolution.
Variable pay components shall be subject to applicable statutory deductions and tax withholding as per prevailing laws.
The company reserves the right to modify or discontinue variable pay schemes with prior notice to employees.
Employees shall not be entitled to variable pay during periods of unpaid leave or suspension unless explicitly stated in their employment agreement.

parents.title: Payroll Policy
parents.breadcrumb: Payroll Policy > Statutory Deductions
parents.text:
## Statutory Deductions
Turabit solutions complies fully with all statutory requirements related to payroll deductions. The primary statutory deductions include Employee Provident Fund (EPF), Employee State Insurance (ESI), Professional Tax, and Income Tax (TDS). These deductions are calculated based on the applicable rates prescribed by government authorities and are deducted from the employee's gross salary each payroll cycle.
Employee Provident Fund contributions are made both by the employee and the employer, with the employee's share deducted from the salary. Employee State Insurance contributions apply to eligible employees and are similarly deducted and matched by the employer. Professional Tax is deducted as per the state government regulations applicable to the employee's location.
Income Tax deductions are computed based on the employee's declared investments, exemptions, and applicable tax slabs. The payroll department ensures timely deposit of all statutory deductions to the respective government bodies and maintains records for audit and compliance purposes. Employees are provided with detailed payslips reflecting all statutory deductions for transparency and record-keeping.

parents.title: Payroll Policy
parents.breadcrumb: Payroll Policy > Investment Declaration and Tax Computation Process
parents.text:
## Investment Declaration and Tax Computation Process
The investment declaration and tax computation process at Turabit Solutions Private Limited is designed to ensure accurate, compliant, and transparent tax deduction at source (TDS) for all eligible employees in accordance with Indian tax regulations. This process begins annually with a provisional declaration phase, where employees are required to submit their projected investment declarations for the financial year by the 15th of April through the Keka HRMS platform. These declarations encompass eligible deductions under various sections of the Income Tax Act, including Section 80C (such as Public Provident Fund, Equity Linked Savings Scheme, Life Insurance premiums, home loan principal repayment, and National Savings Certificates, up to a limit of Rs 1,50,000), Section 80D (health insurance premiums up to Rs 25,000 for self and Rs 50,000 for senior citizen parents), Section 80E (education loan interest), Section 24(b) (home loan interest up to Rs 2,00,000), as well as declarations for House Rent Allowance (HRA) exemption supported by rent receipts and landlord PAN details when annual rent exceeds Rs 1,00,000, and Leave Travel Allowance (LTA) claims. Employees must also select their preferred tax regime--old or new--during this period, with the understanding that this choice remains fixed for the entire financial year.
Following the provisional declaration, employees are required to submit actual investment proofs between January and February, with a deadline of 31st January for uploading documents such as premium receipts, bank statements, PPF passbooks, Form 16A from banks, rent receipts, and home loan certificates. The payroll team reviews these submissions by the 10th of February to verify compliance and accuracy. Based on this review, TDS is recalculated for the full financial year during the February payroll cycle to adjust for any shortfalls or excesses in the provisional deductions. Any shortfall in TDS is recovered through deductions in the February and March payrolls, while any excess TDS is refunded in the March payroll.
Monthly TDS deductions are computed under Section 192 of the Income Tax Act, taking into account the employee's projected annual income, declared investments, HRA exemptions, the standard deduction of Rs 50,000, and the applicable tax slab based on the selected tax regime. This calculation is updated quarterly to reflect any changes in investment proofs or salary revisions. The process ensures that employees' tax liabilities are managed efficiently and transparently throughout the year.
At the conclusion of the financial year, Form 16 is issued to all employees by 15th June, providing a detailed summary of income and tax deductions for the preceding year. This form is made available for download via Keka under the Documents section, facilitating employees' tax filing and compliance.
This structured approach to investment declaration and tax computation supports Turabit Solutions' commitment to maintaining full compliance with statutory tax requirements while providing employees with clear visibility into their tax deductions and benefits. It also enables timely and accurate payroll processing, minimizing discrepancies and ensuring employee confidence in the company's payroll practices.

parents.title: Payroll Policy
parents.breadcrumb: Payroll Policy > Expense Reimbursement Categories and Claim Process
parents.text:
## Expense Reimbursement Categories and Claim Process
Eligible Expense Categories: Employees may submit reimbursement claims for expenses incurred in the course of business activities, subject to prior approvals and policy limits. Eligible categories include business travel expenses such as cab, auto, local train, and bus fares for client visits or office errands. Flights and hotel accommodations require prior written approval from the respective department head and Finance. Mobile and internet expenses are reimbursed up to Rs 500 per month for employees in customer-facing or remote roles as per the approved list maintained by Human Resources. Meals during client entertainment are reimbursable up to Rs 2,000 per instance, provided the claim includes the client's name, purpose of the meeting, and a list of attendees. Certification and training expenses are reimbursed up to Rs 15,000 per financial year against valid invoices for approved courses, requiring pre-approval from the reporting manager. A one-time relocation allowance of Rs 25,000 is payable to new joiners relocating to Pune from another city, disbursed in the first payroll following submission of moving receipts.
Claim Submission Process: Employees must submit expense claims through the Keka HRMS portal under the Reimbursements section, uploading original bills or invoices in PDF or JPEG format. Claims must be submitted within 30 days from the date the expense was incurred. Claims submitted beyond this 30-day window will be rejected unless accompanied by a written waiver from the department head.
Approval Workflow: Upon submission, the reporting manager is responsible for approving the claim within three working days. Following managerial approval, the Finance team reviews and approves the claim within two working days. Only claims approved by both the reporting manager and Finance will be processed for reimbursement.
Reimbursement Timing: Approved claims submitted and fully approved by the 20th of the month will be reimbursed in the same month's payroll cycle. Claims approved after the 20th will be processed in the subsequent month's payroll. This ensures timely and accurate reimbursement aligned with the monthly payroll cycle.

parents.title: Payroll Policy
parents.breadcrumb: Payroll Policy > Payslip Generation, Distribution and Digital Access
parents.text:
## Payslip Generation, Distribution and Digital Access
Payslips at Turabit solutions are generated monthly following the completion of the payroll processing cycle. The payroll system automatically compiles all salary components, statutory deductions, variable pay, and reimbursements into a detailed payslip for each employee. Payslips provide a transparent breakdown of earnings and deductions, enabling employees to verify their compensation accurately.
Distribution of payslips is conducted digitally through the company's secure employee portal. Employees receive notifications when their payslips are available for download, ensuring timely access. The digital format supports confidentiality and reduces paper usage, aligning with the company's sustainability goals.
Employees can access their payslips anytime via the portal, which maintains an archive of past payslips for reference. In case of any discrepancies or issues with payslip details, employees are encouraged to report them promptly to the payroll or HR department for investigation and correction.
The company ensures that payslip data is protected with appropriate security measures to safeguard employee privacy and comply with data protection regulations.

parents.title: Payroll Policy
parents.breadcrumb: Payroll Policy > Advance Salary Request Policy and Recovery Terms
parents.text:
## Advance Salary Request Policy and Recovery Terms
Employees who have completed a minimum of six months of confirmed service at Turabit Solutions Private Limited and have no outstanding advance salary balance shall be eligible to request an advance on their salary. The maximum permissible advance shall not exceed one month's net take-home salary. At no time shall an employee have more than one outstanding advance. Requests for salary advances shall not be entertained during the employee's notice period.
The process for obtaining an advance salary shall require the employee to submit a formal request via email to hr@turabitsolutions.com, clearly stating the reason for the advance, which must be limited to medical emergencies, family emergencies, or relocation expenses. Upon receipt, the Human Resources department shall forward the request to the Finance team to verify the employee's current advance balance and salary eligibility. Approval authority shall be delegated as follows: advances up to Rs 25,000 shall require approval from the HR Manager, while advances exceeding Rs 25,000 shall require approval from the Chief Financial Officer (CFO). The approval decision shall be communicated to the employee within three working days of the request submission. Upon approval, the advance amount shall be credited to the employee's salary account within two working days.
Recovery of the advance salary shall be executed through automatic deductions in equal monthly installments over three consecutive payroll cycles, commencing from the month following the disbursement.
