children.text: ## Investment Declaration and Tax Computation Process The investment declaration and tax computation process at Turabit Solutions Private Limited is designed to ensure accurate, compliant, and transparent tax deduction at source (TDS) for all eligible employees in accordance with Indian tax regulations. This process begins annually with a provisional declaration phase, where employees are required to submit their projected investment declarations for the financial year by the 15th of April through the Keka HRMS platform. These declarations encompass eligible deductions under various sections of the Income Tax Act, including Section 80C (such as Public Provident Fund, Equity Linked Savings Scheme, Life Insurance premiums, home loan principal repayment, and National Savings Certificates, up to a limit of Rs 1,50,000), Section 80D (health insurance premiums up to Rs 25,000 for self and Rs 50,000 for senior citizen parents), Section 80E (education loan interest), Section 24(b) (home loan interest up to Rs 2,00,000), as well as declarations for House Rent Allowance (HRA) exemption supported by rent receipts and landlord PAN details when annual rent exceeds Rs 1,00,000, and Leave Travel Allowance (LTA) claims. Employees must also select their preferred tax regime--old or new--during this period, with the understanding that this choice remains fixed for the entire financial year. Following the provisional declaration, employees are required to submit actual investment proofs between January and February, with a deadline of 31st January for uploading documents such as premium receipts, bank statements, PPF passbooks, Form 16A from banks, rent receipts, and home loan certificates. The payroll team reviews these submissions by the 10th of February to verify compliance and accuracy. Based on this review, TDS is recalculated for the full financial year during the February payroll cycle to adjust for any shortfalls or excesses in the provisional deductions. Any shortfall in TDS is recovered through deductions in the February and March payrolls, while any excess TDS is refunded in the March payroll. Monthly TDS deductions are computed under Section 192 of the Income Tax Act, taking into account the employee's projected annual income, declared investments, HRA exemptions, the standard deduction of Rs 50,000, and the applicable tax slab based on the selected tax regime. This calculation is updated quarterly to reflect any changes in investment proofs or salary revisions. The process ensures that employees' tax liabilities are managed efficiently and transparently throughout the year.

children.text:
## Expense Reimbursement Categories and Claim Process
Eligible Expense Categories: Employees may submit reimbursement claims for expenses incurred in the course of business activities, subject to prior approvals and policy limits. Eligible categories include business travel expenses such as cab, auto, local train, and bus fares for client visits or office errands. Flights and hotel accommodations require prior written approval from the respective department head and Finance. Mobile and internet expenses are reimbursed up to Rs 500 per month for employees in customer-facing or remote roles as per the approved list maintained by Human Resources. Meals during client entertainment are reimbursable up to Rs 2,000 per instance, provided the claim includes the client's name, purpose of the meeting, and a list of attendees. Certification and training expenses are reimbursed up to Rs 15,000 per financial year against valid invoices for approved courses, requiring pre-approval from the reporting manager. A one-time relocation allowance of Rs 25,000 is payable to new joiners relocating to Pune from another city, disbursed in the first payroll following submission of moving receipts.
Claim Submission Process: Employees must submit expense claims through the Keka HRMS portal under the Reimbursements section, uploading original bills or invoices in PDF or JPEG format. Claims must be submitted within 30 days from the date the expense was incurred. Claims submitted beyond this 30-day window will be rejected unless accompanied by a written waiver from the department head.
Approval Workflow: Upon submission, the reporting manager is responsible for approving the claim within three working days. Following managerial approval, the Finance team reviews and approves the claim within two working days. Only claims approved by both the reporting manager and Finance will be processed for reimbursement.
Reimbursement Timing: Approved claims submitted and fully approved by the 20th of the month will be reimbursed in the same month's payroll cycle. Claims approved after the 20th will be processed in the subsequent month's payroll. This ensures timely and accurate reimbursement aligned with the monthly payroll cycle.

children.text:
## Advance Salary Request Policy and Recovery Terms
Employees who have completed a minimum of six months of confirmed service at Turabit Solutions Private Limited and have no outstanding advance salary balance shall be eligible to request an advance on their salary. The maximum permissible advance shall not exceed one month's net take-home salary. At no time shall an employee have more than one outstanding advance. Requests for salary advances shall not be entertained during the employee's notice period.
The process for obtaining an advance salary shall require the employee to submit a formal request via email to hr@turabitsolutions.com, clearly stating the reason for the advance, which must be limited to medical emergencies, family emergencies, or relocation expenses. Upon receipt, the Human Resources department shall forward the request to the Finance team to verify the employee's current advance balance and salary eligibility. Approval authority shall be delegated as follows: advances up to Rs 25,000 shall require approval from the HR Manager, while advances exceeding Rs 25,000 shall require approval from the Chief Financial Officer (CFO). The approval decision shall be communicated to the employee within three working days of the request submission. Upon approval, the advance amount shall be credited to the employee's salary account within two working days.
Recovery of the advance salary shall be executed through automatic deductions in equal monthly installments over three consecutive payroll cycles, commencing from the month following the disbursement. In the event the employee resigns or separates from the company prior to full recovery of the advance, the outstanding balance shall be deducted from the employee's full and final settlement without requiring additional consent. Should the full and final settlement amount be insufficient to cover the outstanding advance, the employee shall be obligated to repay the remaining balance via NEFT transfer within seven days of receiving the full and final settlement statement.
All advance salary transactions shall be documented and maintained in the payroll system to ensure transparency and auditability. Compliance with this policy is mandatory, and any deviations or violations shall be subject to review and appropriate action by the Human Resources and Finance departments.

children.text:
## Salary Revision and Increment Processing Guidelines
Salary revisions and increments at Turabit Solutions Private Limited follow a structured annual cycle commencing on 1st April each year. Eligibility criteria include a minimum of six months confirmed service as of 31st March, a performance rating of 3 or higher in the October appraisal, and absence of any active disciplinary actions on the revision date. Increment percentages are aligned with performance ratings: exceptional (rating 5) receive 20 to 25%, exceeds expectations (rating 4) receive 12 to 18%, meets expectations (rating 3) receive 6 to 10%, while ratings below 3 receive no increment, with mandatory performance improvement plans for rating 1. Increment letters are issued by 30th April, with revised salaries effective from 1st April and arrears for April paid in May payroll. Off-cycle salary revisions are permitted for promotions, CEO-approved counter-offers, and HR-flagged market corrections, requiring CFO and CEO approval, effective from the first day of the month following approval. Department heads must submit increment recommendations to HR by 31st March using the standardized proposal form. HR reviews submissions for internal equity before forwarding to Finance and CEO for final approval. The payroll team updates revised salaries in Keka upon receipt of signed increment letters.

children.text: ## Full and Final Settlement Calculation and Timeline The Full and Final (FnF) settlement process at Turabit Solutions Private Limited is designed to ensure a comprehensive and timely closure of all financial obligations between the company and the employee upon separation, whether by resignation, termination, retirement, or contract completion. The FnF settlement is processed in strict adherence to the company's payroll policy and applicable Indian labour laws, maintaining transparency and accuracy. Upon an employee's last working day, the FnF statement is prepared and issued within 30 calendar days. This statement details all payable components and applicable deductions, providing the employee with a clear overview of the final amount due. The payment of the FnF amount is credited to the employee's registered bank account within 45 calendar days from the last working day, subject to completion of all requisite formalities. The FnF calculation includes several key components. Pending salary is calculated on a per-day basis for the final month worked, using a divisor of 26 days to determine the daily gross salary. Earned leave encashment is computed for all accumulated earned leave balances up to a maximum cap of 24 days, calculated as basic salary divided by 26, multiplied by the number of eligible leave days. Gratuity is payable if the employee's continuous service exceeds five years, calculated as fifteen days' wages per completed year of service, using the last drawn basic salary as the wage basis. Variable pay is pro-rated for the quarter up to the last working day, contingent on the employee meeting KPI targets and company revenue benchmarks. Additionally, any approved pending expense reimbursements and vested retention bonuses are included in the FnF amount. Deductions from the FnF settlement are applied as per policy and statutory requirements. These include any outstanding salary advances, which are recovered in full; salary in lieu of notice period if the employee has not served or has short-served the notice; applicable Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) calculated on all FnF components in accordance with the Income Tax Act; and the value of any unreturned company assets such as laptops or access cards, as recorded in the asset register. Other dues owed to the company are also deducted accordingly. The release of the FnF settlement is contingent upon the employee fulfilling all exit formalities. This includes the return of all company property verified by the IT department, completion of the exit interview, sign-off on knowledge transfer by the reporting manager, and clearance of no-dues certificates from IT, Administration, and Finance departments.

This statement details all payable components and applicable deductions, providing the employee with a clear overview of the final amount due. The payment of the FnF amount is credited to the employee's registered bank account within 45 calendar days from the last working day, subject to completion of all requisite formalities. The FnF calculation includes several key components. Pending salary is calculated on a per-day basis for the final month worked, using a divisor of 26 days to determine the daily gross salary. Earned leave encashment is computed for all accumulated earned leave balances up to a maximum cap of 24 days, calculated as basic salary divided by 26, multiplied by the number of eligible leave days. Gratuity is payable if the employee's continuous service exceeds five years, calculated as fifteen days' wages per completed year of service, using the last drawn basic salary as the wage basis. Variable pay is pro-rated for the quarter up to the last working day, contingent on the employee meeting KPI targets and company revenue benchmarks. Additionally, any approved pending expense reimbursements and vested retention bonuses are included in the FnF amount. Deductions from the FnF settlement are applied as per policy and statutory requirements. These include any outstanding salary advances, which are recovered in full; salary in lieu of notice period if the employee has not served or has short-served the notice; applicable Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) calculated on all FnF components in accordance with the Income Tax Act; and the value of any unreturned company assets such as laptops or access cards, as recorded in the asset register. Other dues owed to the company are also deducted accordingly. The release of the FnF settlement is contingent upon the employee fulfilling all exit formalities. This includes the return of all company property verified by the IT department, completion of the exit interview, sign-off on knowledge transfer by the reporting manager, and clearance of no-dues certificates from IT, Administration, and Finance departments.

children.text:
## Payroll Dispute Escalation and Resolution Process
Employees who identify discrepancies or concerns related to their payroll must follow a structured escalation and resolution process to ensure timely and accurate correction of any errors. The initial step requires employees to conduct a self-service review by carefully examining their payslip available on Keka HRMS. They should cross-reference the payslip details with their offer letter, increment letter, approved leave records, and any other relevant documentation before initiating a dispute. This preliminary verification helps clarify common misunderstandings and reduces unnecessary escalations.
If discrepancies persist after this review, the employee should submit a formal query by emailing payroll@turabitsolutions.com. The email must include the employee ID, the specific payroll month in question, and a detailed description of the issue, supported by relevant documents such as approved leave records, reimbursement approvals, or increment letters. The payroll team commits to responding within three working days, providing clarification or initiating corrective action as necessary.
Should the employee find the response unsatisfactory or if the issue remains unresolved after three working days, the matter should be escalated to the Human Resources Manager by contacting hrmanager@turabitsolutions.com. The HR Manager will review the case within two working days and collaborate with the Finance department to facilitate resolution. This step ensures that more complex or sensitive payroll issues receive appropriate managerial attention.
For disputes involving amounts exceeding Rs 10,000 or those unresolved after HR Manager intervention, escalation to the Chief Financial Officer (CFO) is required. The CFO will conduct a thorough review within three working days to determine the appropriate course of action. This hierarchical escalation framework guarantees that significant payroll discrepancies receive executive-level oversight.
Once a payroll error is confirmed through this process, corrections are typically implemented in the subsequent payroll cycle to ensure accurate salary disbursement. In cases where the error amount exceeds Rs 5,000, the CFO may authorize an off-cycle payment to expedite reimbursement, which will be processed within five working days of error confirmation. All identified errors and their resolutions are meticulously documented in the payroll audit log to maintain transparency and accountability.
Throughout the dispute resolution process, employees will receive written communication via email detailing the outcome and any corrective measures taken. This structured approach reinforces Turabit Solutions' commitment to maintaining a transparent, consistent, and compliant payroll system, thereby fostering employee trust and satisfaction.

## Policy Compliance, Audit Trail and Approval Authority
All payroll activities at Turabit solutions must comply with this policy, applicable labor laws, and tax regulations.
The payroll department shall maintain a comprehensive audit trail of all payroll transactions, including salary calculations, deductions, payments, and approvals.
Regular internal audits shall be conducted to ensure adherence to policy and identify areas for improvement.
Any deviations or exceptions to the policy require documented justification and approval from the designated authority.
The Human Resources Manager holds the primary approval authority for payroll-related policies, salary advances, and revisions.
Senior Management approval is required for salary increments, structural changes, and final settlements.
Employees and managers must cooperate fully during audits and investigations related to payroll.
Non-compliance with this policy may result in disciplinary action, including corrective measures and potential legal consequences.
This policy shall be reviewed annually and updated as necessary to reflect changes in laws, business needs, or best practices.
All employees are responsible for understanding and adhering to the payroll policy to ensure smooth and transparent compensation management.

## Purpose and Scope
The Code of Conduct at Turabit Solutions is designed to establish clear expectations for ethical behavior, professionalism, and compliance across the organization. Its purpose is to guide employees in making responsible decisions that align with the company's values, legal obligations, and industry standards within the SaaS ecosystem. This Code applies to all employees, contractors, consultants, and stakeholders associated with Turabit Solutions, regardless of role, seniority, or geographic location. It governs conduct in all work-related settings, including office environments, remote workspaces, client interactions, digital communications, and any situation where an individual represents the company. By adhering to this Code, all members of Turabit Solutions contribute to a culture of trust, respect, and excellence that supports the company's mission and reputation in the SaaS industry.

## Core Values and Expected Professional Standards
Employees must consistently demonstrate integrity in all actions and decisions, ensuring honesty and ethical conduct at all times.
Employees shall be accountable for their responsibilities, delivering on commitments and accepting ownership of outcomes.
Transparency must be maintained in communications and reporting, fostering trust within teams and with clients.
Customer-centricity shall guide all work, prioritizing client needs and delivering high-quality solutions.
Employees must uphold high standards of professionalism, including respectful behavior, punctuality, and adherence to company policies.
Collaboration is essential; employees shall actively engage with colleagues, valuing diverse perspectives to drive innovation.
Innovation must be encouraged by embracing new ideas and continuous improvement in processes and products.
Compliance with all applicable laws, internal policies, and contractual obligations is mandatory for every employee.
Employees must act in the best interest of Turabit Solutions and its clients, avoiding conflicts and protecting company assets.
Honesty in all communications and decisions is required to maintain the company's reputation and ethical standing.

## Respect, Inclusion and Anti-Discrimination Policy
Turabit Solutions is committed to maintaining a workplace that is inclusive, respectful, and free from discrimination.
Employees must treat all colleagues, clients, and partners with dignity and respect, regardless of race, gender, age, religion, disability, sexual orientation, or any other protected characteristic.
Discriminatory behavior, exclusionary practices, or biased decision-making are strictly prohibited in all forms.
The company promotes equal opportunity in hiring, promotion, and all employment practices to ensure fairness and diversity.
Employees shall foster an environment where diverse perspectives are valued and everyone feels safe to contribute their ideas and talents.
Any incidents or concerns related to discrimination must be reported promptly through appropriate channels for investigation and resolution.
Managers and leaders are responsible for modeling inclusive behavior and addressing any violations of this policy swiftly and effectively.
Training and awareness programs will be provided regularly to reinforce the importance of respect and inclusion within the workplace.

## Anti-Harassment and POSH Policy
Turabit Solutions maintains a zero-tolerance approach toward harassment, including sexual harassment, in accordance with applicable laws such as the Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH) regulations.
Any unwelcome behavior--whether verbal, physical, or digital--that creates a hostile or intimidating work environment is strictly prohibited.
The company has established a formal Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) to address complaints confidentially, fairly, and promptly.
Employees are encouraged to report incidents of harassment without fear of retaliation or adverse consequences.
All complaints will be investigated with due sensitivity, impartiality, and in accordance with legal and company procedures.
Training on harassment prevention and awareness of POSH regulations will be provided regularly to all employees.
Managers must ensure a safe and respectful workplace and take immediate action if harassment is suspected or reported.
Confidentiality will be maintained throughout the complaint and investigation process to protect all parties involved.

children.text:
## Conflict of Interest Disclosure Requirements
Employees must avoid situations where personal interests conflict, or appear to conflict, with the interests of Turabit Solutions.
Conflicts may include financial interests, external employment, personal relationships, or affiliations that could influence professional judgment.
Employees are required to disclose any actual or potential conflicts of interest promptly to their reporting manager or the HR department.
The company will review all disclosures and determine appropriate mitigation measures to ensure transparency and fairness.
Failure to disclose conflicts of interest may result in disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment.
Employees must recuse themselves from decision-making processes where a conflict of interest exists or could be perceived.
Regular training and reminders will be provided to help employees recognize and manage conflicts of interest effectively.
Open communication and honesty are essential to maintaining trust and integrity within the organization.

## Social Media Usage and Public Communication Policy
Employees are expected to use social media responsibly and ensure that their public communications do not harm the reputation of Turabit Solutions.
Unauthorized sharing of confidential information, client data, or internal discussions is strictly prohibited.
When representing the company publicly, employees must ensure that communications are accurate, respectful, and aligned with official messaging.
Personal opinions expressed on social media must be clearly distinguished from the company's positions to avoid confusion.
Employees shall refrain from posting content that could be considered offensive, discriminatory, or damaging to the company's image.
Use of social media during working hours should not interfere with job responsibilities or productivity.
Any social media activity that raises concerns about compliance or ethics must be reported to management or HR.
Training and guidelines will be provided to help employees navigate social media use in a professional and compliant manner.

Regular audits and monitoring may be conducted to ensure compliance with these guidelines, and employees are expected to cooperate fully with such processes.

## Consequences of Misconduct and Disciplinary Framework
Verbal or Written Warnings: For minor infractions or first-time violations, employees may receive verbal or written warnings outlining the issue and expectations for corrective action. This serves as an opportunity to improve behavior without formal penalties.
Suspension: More serious or repeated violations may result in temporary suspension from work duties, with or without pay, while investigations or corrective measures are undertaken. Suspension emphasizes the gravity of the misconduct and allows time for resolution.
Termination of Employment: Severe breaches of the Code of Conduct, including unethical behavior, legal violations, or actions damaging to the company's reputation, may lead to immediate termination of employment in accordance with applicable laws and company policies.
Legal Action: In cases involving criminal conduct, fraud, or other unlawful activities, Turabit Solutions reserves the right to pursue legal action in addition to internal disciplinary measures to protect its interests and comply with legal obligations

Legal Action: In cases involving criminal conduct, fraud, or other unlawful activities, Turabit Solutions reserves the right to pursue legal action in addition to internal disciplinary measures to protect its interests and comply with legal obligations

## Scope and Purpose of Disclosure
The purpose of this Agreement is to ensure that all confidential information disclosed by Turabit solutions to the employee is used solely for legitimate business purposes related to the employee's role within the company. Disclosure of such information is strictly limited to activities necessary for the performance of assigned duties and responsibilities. The employee acknowledges that unauthorized use or disclosure of confidential information could cause significant harm to Turabit solutions, including financial loss and damage to reputation. Therefore, the employee agrees to handle all confidential information with the highest degree of care and discretion. This Agreement governs all forms of disclosure, whether verbal, written, electronic, or otherwise, and applies to all confidential information shared during the course of employment. The employee shall not use the confidential information for any personal gain or for the benefit of any third party without prior written consent from Turabit solutions.

children.text:
## Obligations and Duties of the Receiving Party
6.1 The Receiving Party shall maintain the confidentiality of all Confidential Information received from Turabit solutions and shall not disclose such information to any third party without prior written authorization.
6.2 The Receiving Party must use the Confidential Information solely for the purposes authorized under this Agreement and shall not use it for personal benefit or for the benefit of any other entity.
6.3 The Receiving Party shall take all reasonable measures to protect the confidentiality of the information, including implementing security protocols and restricting access to authorized personnel only.
6.4 The Receiving Party shall promptly notify Turabit solutions in writing upon discovery of any unauthorized use or disclosure of Confidential Information or any other breach of this Agreement.
6.5 The Receiving Party shall not copy, reproduce, or otherwise duplicate Confidential Information except as necessary for authorized business purposes and shall ensure that all copies are marked as confidential.
6.6 The Receiving Party shall comply with all applicable laws and regulations relating to the protection of confidential and personal data.
6.7 Upon termination of employment or upon request by Turabit solutions, the Receiving Party shall return or destroy all materials containing Confidential Information, including all copies, summaries, and extracts.
6.8 The Receiving Party shall ensure that any subcontractors, agents, or affiliates who have access to Confidential Information are bound by confidentiality obligations no less restrictive than those contained in this Agreement.
6.9 The Receiving Party shall not reverse engineer, decompile, or disassemble any software or technology disclosed as Confidential Information.
6.10 The Receiving Party acknowledges that any breach of these obligations may cause irreparable harm to Turabit solutions and agrees that Turabit solutions shall be entitled to seek injunctive relief in addition to any other remedies available at law or equity.

Active participation in daily standups, sprint planning, and retrospectives is also required.

## Probation Period Terms and Confirmation Criteria
The employee shall undergo a probation period of three months commencing from the date of joining, specifically from 19 May 2026 to 18 August 2026. During this period, the employee's performance and suitability for the role will be closely monitored. Confirmation of employment is contingent upon meeting the following criteria: completion of onboarding and tool setup within the first two weeks; independent delivery of at least three sprint tasks within the first six weeks; active participation in code reviews with positive feedback from senior engineers; no unresolved production incidents attributable to the employee; attendance of 95% or higher during the probation period; and a satisfactory written evaluation by the reporting manager, Karan Joshi, assessing technical competency, communication skills, and team collaboration. A formal probation review meeting will be conducted jointly by Human Resources and the reporting manager during the eleventh week. Upon successful completion of the review, a confirmation letter will be issued within seven working days. The company reserves the right to extend the probation period by up to 30 additional days at its discretion, with written notice provided to the employee. Failure to meet the confirmation criteria may result in termination or extension of probation as deemed appropriate by the company.

Confirmation of employment is contingent upon meeting the following criteria: completion of onboarding and tool setup within the first two weeks; independent delivery of at least three sprint tasks within the first six weeks; active participation in code reviews with positive feedback from senior engineers; no unresolved production incidents attributable to the employee; attendance of 95% or higher during the probation period; and a satisfactory written evaluation by the reporting manager, Karan Joshi, assessing technical competency, communication skills, and team collaboration. A formal probation review meeting will be conducted jointly by Human Resources and the reporting manager during the eleventh week. Upon successful completion of the review, a confirmation letter will be issued within seven working days. The company reserves the right to extend the probation period by up to 30 additional days at its discretion, with written notice provided to the employee. Failure to meet the confirmation criteria may result in termination or extension of probation as deemed appropriate by the company.

## Standard Working Hours and Overtime Policy
The standard working hours shall be nine hours per day, inclusive of a one-hour break, from Monday to Friday.
Core working hours are defined as 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM Indian Standard Time (IST), during which the employee must be available and responsive regardless of work location.
The total standard working week comprises 40 hours.
Employees must adhere strictly to the core hours to ensure effective collaboration and communication within the team.
Turabit Solutions does not maintain a formal overtime pay structure for salaried permanent employees, as compensation is fixed and aligned with market standards.
Occasional work beyond standard hours may be required during product releases, client escalations, or critical incidents and is considered part of the employee's role at this level.
Where weekend work is necessary and has received prior written approval from the reporting manager, the employee shall be entitled to a compensatory day off (Comp Off).
Comp Off must be availed within 30 days of the weekend work and requests should be submitted via the Keka HRMS platform for approval by the reporting manager.
Employees shall not undertake overtime work without prior authorization from their reporting manager.
The company expects employees to manage their workload efficiently within standard working hours, utilizing overtime only when exceptional circumstances arise.

## Confidentiality and Non-Disclosure Obligations
The employee shall maintain strict confidentiality of all information pertaining to Turabit Solutions' business operations, clients, source code, product roadmaps, pricing strategies, financial data, personnel information, trade secrets, and any proprietary information accessed during the course of employment. This obligation commences on the date of joining and continues indefinitely after separation from the company, regardless of the reason for termination. The employee shall not disclose, reproduce, or use confidential information for any purpose other than performing their duties under this contract. Confidential information must not be discussed in public spaces, shared via personal devices or personal email accounts, or posted on any social media platforms. The employee is required to report any accidental disclosure of confidential information to the Chief Information Security Officer within 24 hours. Breach of these confidentiality obligations will result in immediate termination and may attract civil and criminal liabilities under applicable laws including the Information Technology Act 2000 and the Indian Contract Act 1872.

## Non-Compete and Non-Solicitation Clause
For a period of 12 months following the date of separation, the employee shall not directly or indirectly engage with, be employed by, consult for, or hold a financial interest in any company that offers products or services that directly compete with Turabit Solutions' core SaaS product lines within India.
This non-compete restriction applies only to companies with annual revenue below Rs 500 crore.
This clause shall not apply if the employee's termination is without cause by the company.
For a period of 24 months following separation, the employee shall not directly or indirectly solicit, recruit, or induce any current employee of Turabit Solutions to leave their employment.
For a period of 12 months following separation, the employee shall not directly or indirectly solicit or approach any client of Turabit Solutions with whom the employee had direct contact during the 12 months preceding separation, for the purpose of offering competing services.
The employee acknowledges that these restrictions are reasonable and necessary to protect the legitimate business interests of Turabit Solutions.
Any breach of these obligations may result in legal action including injunctive relief.

## Termination Conditions, Notice Period and Severance
Either party may terminate this employment by providing written notice to the other party. For employees within their first year of confirmed service, the notice period is 30 days. For employees with more than one year of confirmed service, the notice period is 60 days. Notice may be served via email to hr@turabitsolutions.com and must be confirmed in writing. The company reserves the right to waive the notice period and instead pay salary in lieu of notice. Termination for cause, including but not limited to gross misconduct, fraud, theft, breach of confidentiality, willful insubordination, conviction of a criminal offence, or sustained poor performance after a formal performance improvement plan, may be effected without notice or severance. Termination without cause requires payment of salary in lieu of notice. Resignation by the employee requires written notice as specified; failure to serve the notice period entitles the company to recover the equivalent salary from the employee's full and final settlement. Upon termination for any reason, the employee must return all company property on the last working day. Full and final settlement will be processed within 45 days of the last working day. No contractual severance beyond statutory obligations applies unless specifically agreed in writing at the time of separation.

## Governing Law, Jurisdiction and Dispute Resolution
This contract shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of India. Any dispute, claim, or controversy arising out of or in connection with this contract shall first be subject to mandatory mediation for a period of 30 days. If mediation fails to resolve the dispute, the matter shall be submitted to binding arbitration under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act 1996, conducted by a sole arbitrator mutually agreed upon by both parties. The seat of arbitration shall be Pune, Maharashtra, and the language of arbitration shall be English. Notwithstanding the foregoing, either party may seek interim injunctive relief from the competent courts located in Pune. The courts of Pune, Maharashtra shall have exclusive jurisdiction over all matters not resolved through arbitration.

children.text:
## Purpose and Legal Basis
The leave policy at Turabit solutions is designed to provide employees with a structured, fair, and predictable framework for taking time off. This supports their health, personal obligations, and overall work-life balance while ensuring that business operations continue smoothly without disruption. By standardizing leave entitlements across the organization, the policy reduces ad-hoc leave requests and promotes consistent decision-making by managers. This consistency helps maintain fairness and transparency in leave management.
The policy is grounded in applicable legal frameworks including the Factories Act 1948, Shops and Establishments Act (Maharashtra) 2017, Maternity Benefit Act 1961, Payment of Gratuity Act 1972, and relevant provisions of the Code on Social Security 2020. These laws provide the statutory foundation for various leave types and entitlements, ensuring compliance with national labor standards.
By aligning company leave practices with these legal requirements, Turabit solutions ensures that employee rights are protected while balancing organizational needs. The policy also clarifies the roles and responsibilities of employees, managers, and HR in the leave application and approval process, fostering a culture of accountability and mutual respect.

## Scope and Applicability
This leave policy applies comprehensively to all full-time permanent employees, fixed-term contract employees on a pro-rated basis, and interns engaged with Turabit solutions. Part-time employees are covered only for statutory leaves as mandated by law. The policy is applicable across all organizational levels, from interns through to the C-suite executives, ensuring uniformity in leave management practices.
Contractual consultants and third-party vendors engaged through external agencies are explicitly excluded from this policy. The policy governs all employees based in India, regardless of their work arrangement, whether on-site, hybrid, or fully remote. This inclusive approach ensures that all eligible employees receive consistent leave benefits and understand their entitlements and obligations.
By defining clear applicability, the policy supports operational clarity and legal compliance. It also facilitates equitable treatment of employees while accommodating the diverse nature of employment contracts and work modalities within the company.

children.text:
## Leave Types Defined
Earned Leave (EL): Paid leave accrued monthly, intended for planned absences, vacations, or personal needs. Employees must apply for a minimum of one day per instance.
Sick Leave (SL): Paid leave granted for illness or medical procedures. A medical certificate is required for absences exceeding two consecutive days.
Casual Leave (CL): Paid leave for urgent personal matters, limited to a maximum of two consecutive days per instance. Casual leave cannot be combined with earned leave.
Maternity Leave: Fully paid leave of 26 weeks for the first two children as per the Maternity Benefit Act 1961, and 12 weeks for the third child onwards.
Paternity Leave: Five working days of paid leave to be taken within 30 days of the child's birth or adoption.
Bereavement Leave: Three days of paid leave for immediate family members including spouse, child, parent, or sibling; one day for extended family members.
Marriage Leave: Three days of paid leave granted once during the entire employment tenure.
Compensatory Off (Comp Off): Leave earned for working on weekends or public holidays with prior written approval. Must be used within 30 days of earning.
Loss of Pay (LOP): Unpaid leave granted when all other leave balances are exhausted or when specifically requested by the employee.
Adoption Leave: Twelve weeks of paid leave for legally adopting a child below three months of age.

## Annual Leave Entitlement by Employee Category
Full-time permanent employees are entitled to 12 days of Earned Leave, 6 days of Sick Leave, 6 days of Casual Leave, and 12 public holidays per calendar year. Fixed-term contract employees receive leave on a pro-rated basis according to contract duration, with a minimum of 1 Earned Leave day per completed month of service.
Probationary employees are entitled only to 6 Casual Leave and 6 Sick Leave days during probation; Earned Leave accrues from day one but can be availed only after confirmation. Interns receive 1 Casual Leave day per month of internship, with no Earned or Sick Leave unless the internship exceeds six months. Part-time employees are eligible only for statutory leaves, including Sick Leave and public holidays on a pro-rated basis.

Step 5: HR is automatically notified for leaves exceeding five days, Loss of Pay requests, and maternity or paternity leave.
Step 6: The employee receives email confirmation with the updated leave balance. Retrospective leave applications are permitted only in emergencies and require manager and HR approval with written justification.

children.text:
## Carry Forward Rules and Maximum Accumulation Limits
Earned Leave (EL) carry forward: Employees shall be allowed to carry forward a maximum of 6 days of Earned Leave from one calendar year to the next. This carry forward is credited automatically on the 1st of January each year.
Sick Leave (SL) and Casual Leave (CL) shall not be carried forward and will lapse at the end of each calendar year.
Compensatory Off (Comp Off) must be availed within 30 days of earning; any unused Comp Off shall lapse after this period.
The maximum accumulation cap for Earned Leave at any point in time shall be 24 days. Any Earned Leave balance exceeding 24 days shall be automatically lapsed and will not be eligible for encashment unless the employee is undergoing separation from the company.
Employees must monitor their leave balances to avoid loss of entitlement due to lapsing. HR shall provide periodic leave balance statements to employees.
Exceptions to the carry forward and accumulation limits may be considered only in cases of separation, where accumulated Earned Leave up to the cap is eligible for encashment as per company policy.
All carry forward and accumulation rules shall be enforced consistently to maintain fairness and operational efficiency across the organization.

children.text:
## Leave Encashment Policy and Conditions
Earned Leave (EL) encashment is permitted only in two scenarios: at the time of full and final settlement upon employee separation, and during the annual encashment window held in November each year.
Upon separation, all accumulated Earned Leave up to the 24-day cap shall be encashed at the rate calculated as (Basic Salary divided by 26) multiplied by the number of days encashed.
During the annual encashment window, employees may encash up to six Earned Leave days if their balance exceeds 12 days.
Encashment payments are subject to tax deduction at source as applicable under prevailing tax laws.
Sick Leave, Casual Leave, Compensatory Off, and statutory leaves are not eligible for encashment under any circumstances.
Employees must apply for annual encashment within the specified window; late applications will not be entertained.
The company reserves the right to verify leave balances and eligibility before processing encashment payments.
Encashment shall not affect the employee's leave accrual or carry forward entitlements except as explicitly stated in this policy.

children.text:
## Leave During Probation Period
During the probation period, which typically spans the first three months of employment, employees are entitled to 6 Casual Leave (CL) and 6 Sick Leave (SL) days on a pro-rated basis. Earned Leave (EL) begins accruing from the first day of employment; however, it cannot be availed during probation and becomes available only after successful confirmation. No leave balances, including CL and SL, shall be carried forward beyond the probation period.
Maternity, paternity, and bereavement leaves are applicable during probation as mandated by statute and company policy. Excessive leave usage during probation, defined as more than four days of leave in total over the three-month period excluding statutory leaves, will be flagged during the probation review process. Such instances may result in an extension of the probation period by an equivalent number of days to compensate for the absence.
This approach ensures that probationary employees maintain adequate attendance while balancing their health and personal needs. It also provides a clear framework for managing leave during this critical evaluation phase, supporting both employee welfare and organizational requirements.

children.text:
## Leave Abuse Definition and Consequences
Leave abuse at Turabit solutions is defined as any misuse or manipulation of the leave system that undermines fairness and operational efficiency. Examples include consistently taking unplanned leaves on Mondays or Fridays, with a pattern of three or more instances in a quarter; repeated sick leave without valid medical documentation; applying for leave retrospectively without a genuine emergency; misrepresenting the reason for leave; and exceeding approved leave dates without obtaining an extension approval.
Consequences for leave abuse are progressive and designed to correct behavior while maintaining discipline. The first instance results in a written warning issued by HR. A second instance triggers a formal show cause notice and may lead to conversion of disputed leave days to Loss of Pay. A third instance involves a disciplinary committee review, which may result in suspension or termination of employment.
HR monitors leave patterns quarterly and shares reports with department heads to ensure timely identification and management of leave abuse. This policy promotes responsible leave usage and protects the interests of both employees and the organization.

children.text:
## Policy Review Schedule and Approval
The leave policy at Turabit Solutions shall be reviewed on an annual basis every January to ensure its continued relevance, compliance, and effectiveness. The Human Resources Manager shall lead the review process in consultation with department heads and the Finance team to incorporate operational insights and financial considerations. Any updates or revisions to the policy shall be subject to final approval by the CEO, Aangi Shah, before implementation. In addition to the scheduled annual review, the policy shall be subject to trigger-based reviews whenever there is a change in applicable legislation, a significant shift in workforce composition, or in the event of a merger or acquisition. These trigger-based reviews shall be conducted promptly to ensure that the policy remains aligned with legal requirements and organizational needs.
Once the policy has been reviewed and approved, the updated version shall be communicated to all employees via the HRMS notification system and email within seven working days of approval. Employees shall be required to acknowledge receipt and understanding of the updated policy through the HRMS platform within fifteen days of notification. This acknowledgment shall serve as confirmation of their awareness and acceptance of the policy terms. The review and approval process shall be documented and maintained by the Human Resources department to ensure transparency and accountability. The organization shall strictly adhere to this schedule and process to maintain a structured, fair, and legally compliant leave framework that supports employee well-being and business continuity.

Employment at Turabit Solutions is offered under several distinct types to accommodate the diverse needs of our workforce. Additionally, part-time roles are available for select functions, subject to prior approval from Human Resources.

Customer success and sales teams primarily operate on-site to maintain close client engagement. Senior roles may have flexible work arrangements, subject to agreement with their manager. For contractual hires based outside Pune, fully remote work options are available.
These employment types and work arrangements reflect our commitment to fostering a productive and supportive environment where employees can contribute effectively while balancing their professional and personal responsibilities. We encourage open communication with managers and HR to ensure that work arrangements meet both individual and company needs.
All employees are expected to adhere to their designated work schedules and maintain consistent communication regarding their availability. Any requests for changes to employment type or work arrangement should be directed to Human Resources for review and approval.

## Compensation Structure and Payroll Schedule
At Turabit Solutions, our compensation structure is designed to recognize your contributions and align your performance with the company's success. Your total cost to company (CTC) comprises several components to ensure a balanced and motivating remuneration package. The fixed base salary accounts for 60% of your CTC, providing a stable income foundation. In addition, you are eligible for a performance bonus of up to 20% of your CTC, which is paid quarterly and directly linked to individual key performance indicators (KPIs) as well as overall company revenue targets. This variable pay component encourages ownership and accountability, reflecting our core value of acting like a founder rather than a passenger. Alongside these, your CTC includes a special allowance and the company's contribution to your Provident Fund, supporting your long-term financial security.
Payroll processing is conducted with punctuality and reliability. Salaries are credited on the 28th of each month. In cases where the 28th falls on a weekend or a public holiday, payments will be made on the preceding working day to ensure timely receipt of your salary. This consistent schedule supports your financial planning and reflects our commitment to operational excellence.
Our compensation approach is closely tied to performance management. Each employee's quarterly objectives and key results (OKRs) are established in collaboration with their manager. Achieving at least 80% of these OKRs consistently, maintaining zero unresolved customer escalations, and actively participating in team rituals are key expectations that influence your variable pay and promotion opportunities. This system fosters continuous improvement and customer obsession, two of our culture pillars.
We believe that transparent and fair compensation, combined with clear performance expectations and timely payroll, creates an environment where you can focus on delivering value and growing professionally. Should you have any questions regarding your salary components or payroll schedule, please reach out to the Human Resources team for clarification.

In addition, you are eligible for a performance bonus of up to 20% of your CTC, which is paid quarterly and directly linked to individual key performance indicators (KPIs) as well as overall company revenue targets. This variable pay component encourages ownership and accountability, reflecting our core value of acting like a founder rather than a passenger. Alongside these, your CTC includes a special allowance and the company's contribution to your Provident Fund, supporting your long-term financial security.
Payroll processing is conducted with punctuality and reliability. Salaries are credited on the 28th of each month. In cases where the 28th falls on a weekend or a public holiday, payments will be made on the preceding working day to ensure timely receipt of your salary. This consistent schedule supports your financial planning and reflects our commitment to operational excellence.
Our compensation approach is closely tied to performance management. Each employee's quarterly objectives and key results (OKRs) are established in collaboration with their manager. Achieving at least 80% of these OKRs consistently, maintaining zero unresolved customer escalations, and actively participating in team rituals are key expectations that influence your variable pay and promotion opportunities. This system fosters continuous improvement and customer obsession, two of our culture pillars.
We believe that transparent and fair compensation, combined with clear performance expectations and timely payroll, creates an environment where you can focus on delivering value and growing professionally. Should you have any questions regarding your salary components or payroll schedule, please reach out to the Human Resources team for clarification.

children.text:
## Leave and Attendance Policy Summary
Employees shall be entitled to a total of 12earned leave days annually, which shall accrue on a monthly basis. Earned leave may be carried forward up to a maximum of 6 days into the following year. In addition, employees shall receive 6 casual or sick leave days per year, which are non-cumulative and must be utilized within the calendar year. The company recognizes twelve designated public holidays each year, which employees shall observe in accordance with the official holiday calendar.
All leave requests must be submitted through the Human Resource Management System (HRMS) with a minimum of two days' advance notice for planned absences. Attendance shall be monitored through biometric systems and remote check-in procedures to ensure accurate tracking. Employees must maintain regular attendance and provide valid explanations for any absences. Should an employee incur more than three unexplained absences within a single quarter, a formal review process shall be initiated to address the issue.
It is the obligation of every employee to adhere strictly to these leave and attendance requirements to maintain operational efficiency and team coordination. Failure to comply with the leave request procedures or attendance policies may result in disciplinary action as outlined in the company's disciplinary process. Employees are expected to plan their leave responsibly, ensuring minimal disruption to their work and team commitments.
Turabit Solutions shall enforce these policies consistently to uphold fairness and transparency across all departments. Employees shall remain responsible for monitoring their leave balances and ensuring compliance with the company's attendance standards. The Human Resources department shall provide support and guidance regarding leave entitlements and attendance tracking as needed.

## Performance Expectations and Review Cycle
At Turabit solutions, we maintain clear performance expectations to foster professional growth and organizational success. Employees are expected to meet the objectives and responsibilities outlined in their job descriptions while demonstrating commitment, initiative, and collaboration. Performance reviews are conducted on a regular cycle, typically annually, with interim feedback sessions as needed. These reviews provide an opportunity to assess achievements, identify areas for improvement, and set goals for the upcoming period. The process is designed to be transparent, constructive, and supportive, encouraging open dialogue between employees and their managers. Performance metrics are aligned with company goals and individual roles, ensuring relevance and fairness. Employees are encouraged to actively participate in their development by seeking feedback, pursuing training, and aligning their efforts with team and company priorities. This structured approach to performance management helps recognize contributions, address challenges, and support career advancement within Turabit solutions.

## Code of Conduct and Workplace Behavior
Turabit solutions is committed to maintaining a professional, respectful, and inclusive workplace. All employees are expected to adhere to the highest standards of conduct, demonstrating integrity, respect, and accountability in their interactions. Discrimination, harassment, or any form of inappropriate behavior is strictly prohibited and will be addressed promptly and fairly. Employees shall comply with all company policies, legal requirements, and ethical guidelines while performing their duties. Confidentiality and respect for company property and resources are essential. Collaboration and open communication are encouraged to foster a positive work environment. Employees must avoid conflicts of interest and disclose any situations that may compromise their impartiality. Compliance with safety regulations and reporting of unsafe conditions are mandatory. By upholding these principles, we ensure a workplace where everyone can contribute effectively and feel valued. Violations of the code of conduct may result in disciplinary action, including termination, depending on the severity of the offense.

## Disciplinary Process and Grievance Mechanism
Turabit solutions follows a fair and transparent disciplinary process to address employee conduct and performance issues. When concerns arise, the company will investigate the matter thoroughly and provide the employee an opportunity to respond. Disciplinary actions may range from verbal warnings to written warnings, suspension, or termination, depending on the severity and frequency of the issue. The process aims to correct behavior and support improvement while maintaining workplace standards. Employees who believe they have been treated unfairly or have grievances related to their employment are encouraged to raise their concerns through the established grievance mechanism. This includes reporting to immediate supervisors, Human Resources, or designated grievance officers. All complaints will be handled confidentially and impartially, with timely resolution efforts. Retaliation against employees who raise grievances in good faith is strictly prohibited. The company is committed to fostering a respectful environment where issues can be addressed constructively and fairly.

children.text:
## Separation Policy and Exit Process
Employees shall provide a written resignation notice of at least 30 calendar days prior to their intended last working day. For senior roles, this notice period shall be extended to 60 calendar days. The company reserves the right to initiate termination by providing a minimum of 30 calendar days' notice or payment in lieu of notice, except in cases involving gross misconduct, where immediate termination may occur without notice.
Upon separation, employees must complete a formal exit process which includes the thorough transfer of knowledge and responsibilities to designated colleagues or successors. All company property, including but not limited to hardware, software, access cards, and confidential documents, shall be returned in good condition before the final clearance is granted. Access to company systems and networks shall be revoked promptly upon the employee's last working day.
The full and final settlement of all dues, including salary, bonuses, and any applicable reimbursements, shall be processed and paid within 45 calendar days following the employee's last working day. An experience letter confirming the period of employment and role shall be issued within seven working days after the completion of the exit clearance process.
Employees must comply fully with these separation obligations to ensure a smooth transition and maintain the integrity of Turabit Solutions' operations. Failure to adhere to these requirements may delay final settlements or affect the issuance of employment verification documents. The company expects all departing employees to uphold the same standards of professionalism and integrity during the exit process as demonstrated throughout their tenure.

children.text:
## Purpose, Scope and Expansion Revenue Impact on NRR
At Turabit Solutions, this Expansion Revenue Playbook establishes a structured and repeatable methodology to drive revenue growth from our existing customer base. It is designed to empower Customer Success and Sales teams with clear guidance to systematically identify, qualify, and convert expansion opportunities, ensuring that all growth initiatives are closely aligned with delivering measurable customer value. The playbook encompasses all expansion activities across active customers, including upselling to higher-tier plans, cross-selling complementary products, and usage-based growth across all SaaS product lines and customer segments. It covers the entire lifecycle from opportunity identification through deal closure and billing updates, providing a comprehensive framework for consistent execution. Expansion revenue is a critical lever for enhancing Net Revenue Retention (NRR) at Turabit Solutions. While renewals maintain the existing Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR), expansion revenue drives incremental growth, enabling NRR to surpass 100%. This strong expansion motion reduces reliance on new customer acquisition, reflecting deep product adoption, high customer satisfaction, and long-term partnership value.

## Expansion Revenue Types
Upsell: This type involves moving customers to higher-tier subscription plans that offer enhanced features, greater capacity, or additional benefits. Upselling focuses on increasing the value delivered to the customer by upgrading their existing package to better meet evolving needs.
Cross-sell: Cross-selling refers to introducing complementary products, modules, or services that extend the platform's capabilities. This approach broadens the customer's use of Turabit Solutions' ecosystem, driving additional revenue through product diversification.
Usage-based Expansion: This occurs when customers increase their consumption beyond contracted limits, resulting in higher billing. It reflects organic growth driven by increased adoption and reliance on the platform's features and services.
Add-on Expansion: Add-on expansion includes the purchase of additional features, integrations, or professional services that enhance the core product experience. These add-ons provide tailored solutions addressing specific customer requirements.

children.text:
## Expansion Playbook by Trigger Type and Customer Segment
The Expansion Playbook at Turabit Solutions is designed to provide a detailed, actionable framework tailored to specific trigger types and customer segments. For upsell triggers, such as customers nearing capacity limits or requiring advanced features, the playbook recommends proactive engagement by Customer Success Managers (CSMs) to assess needs and coordinate with Sales to present higher-tier plans.
Cross-sell opportunities arise when customers express interest in complementary products or when usage data reveals gaps in their current solution. In these cases, targeted campaigns and personalized demos are employed to showcase relevant modules. Usage-based expansion is driven by monitoring consumption patterns; when thresholds are exceeded, automated alerts prompt CSMs to initiate conversations about scaling plans or add-ons. Add-on expansions focus on identifying customers with specialized requirements, such as integrations or professional services, and involve consultative selling approaches.
The playbook segments customers by size, industry, and product usage maturity to tailor messaging and timing. Enterprise customers receive dedicated account management with quarterly strategic reviews, while mid-market segments benefit from a mix of automated and human touchpoints. Small business customers are engaged through scalable digital campaigns and self-service options. This structured approach ensures that expansion efforts are aligned with customer needs, maximizing conversion rates and revenue growth while maintaining high satisfaction levels.

Turabit Solutions offers a tiered pricing and packaging structure designed to accommodate varying customer needs and facilitate seamless upgrades. The entry-level plan provides essential features with limited capacity, ideal for small teams or early-stage adoption. The mid-tier plan expands feature access, user limits, and includes select add-ons, targeting growing businesses requiring more robust capabilities. The enterprise tier delivers full platform functionality, advanced integrations, and premium support, tailored for large organizations with complex requirements. Upgrade paths are clearly defined to enable customers to move between tiers with minimal friction, supported by transparent pricing and flexible billing options. Add-ons and usage-based pricing components complement the core plans, allowing customers to customize their subscriptions based on evolving demands. This structured approach ensures clarity, scalability, and alignment with customer value realization throughout the expansion journey.

## Proof of Value and ROI Documentation for Expansion Conversations
Providing clear proof of value and demonstrating return on investment (ROI) are essential components of successful expansion conversations at Turabit Solutions. CSMs should leverage quantitative data such as usage analytics, performance improvements, and cost savings realized by the customer to build a compelling business case. Case studies, testimonials, and benchmark reports further reinforce credibility. ROI documentation includes detailed calculations of productivity gains, revenue impact, and efficiency improvements attributable to the expanded solution. This evidence supports transparent discussions about pricing and investment justification, helping customers understand the tangible benefits of upgrading or adding new capabilities. Additionally, customized dashboards and reports are provided to customers to continuously track value realization post-expansion, fostering trust and long-term partnership.

## Objection Handling Guide for Expansion and Upsell Scenarios
Common objections during expansion and upsell discussions include concerns about budget constraints, perceived lack of immediate need, and uncertainty about additional value. The guide recommends addressing budget concerns by highlighting flexible pricing options and phased expansion approaches. For perceived lack of need, CSMs should revisit customer goals and demonstrate how expanded features align with their strategic objectives. When customers express uncertainty, providing proof of value, ROI data, and success stories can build confidence. Active listening, empathy, and collaborative problem-solving are emphasized to overcome resistance and maintain positive relationships throughout the expansion process.

children.text:
## Expansion Deal Handoff, Contract Amendment and Billing Process
The handoff process for expansion deals at Turabit Solutions is designed to ensure a smooth transition from sales closure to implementation and billing. Once an expansion deal is finalized, Sales formally notifies Customer Success and Finance teams with all relevant contract details. Contract amendments are prepared to reflect new terms, pricing, and service levels, requiring review and approval by legal and finance departments. The billing system is updated promptly to incorporate changes, including new subscription tiers, add-ons, or usage-based charges. Customer Success Managers coordinate with implementation teams to schedule onboarding or training sessions as needed. Clear documentation and communication throughout this process minimize errors and delays, ensuring customers experience seamless service continuity and accurate invoicing.
| Phase | Activity | Owner | Due Date |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Deal Closure | Sales notifies Customer Success and Finance with contract details | Sales | Within 1 business day of deal closure |
| Contract Amendment | Prepare and review contract changes for new terms and pricing | Legal and Finance | Within 3 business days of notification |
| Billing Update | Update billing system to reflect expansion charges | Finance | Within 5 business days of contract amendment approval |
| Implementation Coordination | Schedule onboarding and training for expanded features | Customer Success | Within 7 business days of deal closure |

## Expansion Metrics and Reporting Cadence
Turabit Solutions tracks a comprehensive set of metrics to measure the effectiveness of expansion initiatives and inform continuous improvement. Key performance indicators include Net Revenue Retention (NRR), expansion revenue as a percentage of total ARR, average deal size for expansion transactions, and conversion rates from identified signals to closed deals. Usage growth and customer engagement scores are also monitored to assess adoption trends. Reporting cadence is established with monthly dashboards for operational teams, quarterly business reviews with executive leadership, and ad hoc deep dives for strategic planning. This data-driven approach enables timely identification of risks and opportunities, ensuring that expansion efforts remain aligned with company growth objectives and customer success outcomes.

## Purpose, Scope and Role of Customer Sentiment in Retention
At Turabit Solutions, measuring customer sentiment is a fundamental driver of retention strategies as it delivers direct insights into how customers perceive the value, experience, and quality of support provided. While usage data reveals what actions customers take within the product, sentiment analysis explains the underlying reasons for their behavior. This understanding is crucial for anticipating churn risks and identifying opportunities for account expansion. The framework outlined herein encompasses the systematic capture, analysis, and application of customer feedback throughout the entire customer lifecycle, from initial onboarding through to renewal. Its primary objectives are to proactively detect dissatisfaction, enhance the overall customer experience, fortify customer relationships, and ultimately improve retention rates alongside Net Revenue Retention (NRR). Furthermore, this framework establishes a continuous feedback loop that informs and refines product development, support services, and customer success initiatives, ensuring alignment with evolving customer needs and expectations.

children.text:
## NPS Program Design
The Net Promoter Score (NPS) program at Turabit Solutions is designed as a relationship-level metric to gauge customer loyalty rather than a transactional measure. The program centers on a standardized NPS question that asks customers to rate the likelihood of recommending the product to others, followed by an open-ended question to capture qualitative insights. Responses are categorized into promoters, passives, and detractors, with results linked to detailed customer profiles, product usage data, and revenue metrics to provide a comprehensive view of customer sentiment. Surveys are strategically triggered at critical lifecycle milestones such as post-onboarding and prior to renewal, ensuring alignment with key customer engagement points. Integration with the company's CRM and analytics platforms is essential to enable actionable insights and facilitate timely interventions. This design supports a robust understanding of customer loyalty drivers and informs targeted retention and growth strategies.

## CSAT Survey Design, Trigger Points and Frequency
Customer Satisfaction (CSAT) surveys at Turabit Solutions are transactional in nature and tied directly to specific customer interactions. These surveys are triggered following key events such as support ticket resolution, completion of onboarding, training sessions, and after major feature releases. The survey design emphasizes simplicity and focus, typically comprising a satisfaction rating scale question accompanied by an optional comment field to capture additional feedback. To prevent survey fatigue and maintain high-quality response rates, the frequency of CSAT surveys is carefully managed, ensuring customers are not overwhelmed while still providing meaningful data. This balanced approach enables the collection of reliable feedback that reflects the immediate customer experience and supports continuous improvement in service delivery.

## Customer Effort Score Measurement for Support Interactions
Customer Effort Score (CES) measurement at Turabit Solutions is conducted immediately following support interactions to evaluate the ease with which customers resolve their issues. The core survey question focuses on the level of effort required, utilizing a clear and straightforward rating scale. CES serves as a critical operational metric by identifying friction points within support processes, such as prolonged resolution times, complex workflows, or unclear communication. Insights derived from CES data enable the Customer Success and Support teams to streamline processes and reduce customer effort, which strongly correlates with higher retention rates. By prioritizing low-effort experiences, Turabit Solutions enhances customer satisfaction and loyalty, reinforcing the overall customer success strategy.

## Survey Distribution Channels and Timing Strategy
To maximize survey reach and response rates, Turabit Solutions employs a multi-channel distribution strategy that includes email invitations, in-app notifications, and embedded prompts within the product interface. Timing is a critical factor in this approach; surveys are dispatched shortly after key customer interactions to ensure the experience remains fresh in the respondent's mind. For instance, CSAT surveys are triggered immediately following the closure of support tickets, while NPS surveys are scheduled periodically or aligned with significant lifecycle milestones such as onboarding completion or renewal discussions. This timing strategy balances relevance with user convenience, minimizing disruption while encouraging meaningful participation. The combination of diverse channels and carefully timed delivery enhances the effectiveness of the feedback program and supports comprehensive sentiment measurement.

## Response Rate Benchmarks and Improvement Tactics
At Turabit Solutions, response rate targets are set to be both realistic and ambitious, recognizing the differing nature of NPS and CSAT surveys. NPS surveys typically aim for moderate response rates given their relationship-level focus, whereas CSAT surveys generally achieve higher participation due to their transactional context. To improve response rates, the program employs several tactics including keeping surveys concise and focused, personalizing invitation messages, sending timely reminders, and clearly communicating the value and impact of customer feedback. Additionally, closing the feedback loop by demonstrating how input leads to tangible actions encourages ongoing engagement. The Customer Success team is responsible for implementing these tactics with a timeline of quarterly reviews to assess effectiveness and adjust strategies accordingly.

## NPS Score Calculation, Segmentation and Benchmarking
The Net Promoter Score at Turabit Solutions is calculated by subtracting the percentage of detractors from the percentage of promoters within the survey responses. To derive actionable insights, scores are segmented by customer tier, industry vertical, product usage patterns, and lifecycle stage. This segmentation enables a nuanced understanding of loyalty drivers and areas requiring attention. This segmentation enables a nuanced understanding of loyalty drivers and areas requiring attention. Benchmarking is conducted against both historical internal data and relevant SaaS industry standards, allowing the company to track progress over time and identify performance gaps. NPS results are typically reviewed on a monthly or quarterly basis, reflecting their role as a relationship-level indicator. Reports are distributed to key stakeholders including Customer Success leadership, product management teams, support departments, and executive management. This broad distribution fosters cross-functional alignment and collaboration, ensuring that customer feedback drives continuous improvement across the organization. The reporting framework supports transparency and accountability in managing customer experience initiatives.

## Training Content Library Structure and Ownership
The training content library at Turabit Solutions is organized into a modular and scalable framework to facilitate easy access, update, and management. It is segmented into core categories including Onboarding, Feature Deep Dives, Certification Materials, and Continuous Learning Resources. Each category contains a variety of content types such as video tutorials, step-by-step guides, interactive simulations, FAQs, and case studies. Ownership of the content library is distributed across specialized teams to ensure accuracy, relevance, and alignment with product updates. The Customer Success Enablement team is responsible for curating onboarding and continuous learning materials, while the Product Management team oversees feature-specific content to maintain technical precision. The Learning and Development team manages certification program content, ensuring instructional design best practices are applied. A centralized content management system supports version control, metadata tagging, and user access tracking, enabling efficient content lifecycle management. This structure ensures that customers receive up-to-date, role-appropriate training materials that support their journey from initial adoption to advanced usage.
